# Find which slide draws the objections

*Aug 12, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Meet notes now capture the slide on screen. Log each objection against that slide and the weak spots in your deck show up in a week.

## TL;DR
- Since August 3, Meet’s Take notes for me can embed screenshots of presented content, such as slides, in the notes doc.
- That ties what was said to the slide on screen. Log each objection with the slide it came up on.
- A simple Objections tab plus COUNTIFS shows which slides draw pushback.
- Presenters are notified and can turn capture off. Tell prospects notes are being taken.

## Call notes lose the slide

Call notes say “pricing concern” or “asked about SSO.” They rarely say which slide was up. So when product marketing asks which part of the deck isn’t working, the answer is a guess.
On August 3, Google started including screenshots of presented content in Meet’s meeting notes (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/08/visual-screenshots-now-included-in-Google-Meet-meeting-notes.html). When you present during a call with **Take notes for me** on, Gemini can capture slides, charts and diagrams into the notes document, next to the summary. Now the notes know which slide was on screen.

[Figure: Meeting notes with a captured slide. Mockup.]

## Before the call

- **Present from Slides inside Meet.** Screenshots cover presented content.
- **Number your slides** and give each a short title in the speaker notes or on the slide. A screenshot is easier to log when the slide says “7 · Pricing.”
- **Tell the prospect notes are being taken.** Meet notifies the presenter that Gemini may capture screenshots, and the feature can be turned off from the notes panel. Admins can also require consent before notes start.

## After the call: one row per objection

Open the notes doc. For each objection, add a row to an Objections tab in your deck-feedback sheet.

[Figure: One row per objection, keyed to the slide. Mockup.]

- **Slide:** the number and title from the screenshot.
- **Objection:** one plain sentence. “Thinks SSO costs extra.”
- **Category:** a short fixed list: price, security, fit, proof, competitor, timing.
- **Quote:** the prospect’s words, if the notes have them.

Gemini in the Docs side panel can draft this for you from the notes. Ask for a table with those columns, then check each row against the notes before you paste it.

## Count by slide

On a Summary tab, list the slides and count:

    =COUNTIFS(Objections!C:C, A2)

Add a colour scale to the count column and you have a heat map of the deck. After ten calls the pattern is usually obvious: one or two slides draw most of the pushback.

[Figure: Objections per slide after ten calls. Illustrative numbers.]

Read the hot slides with the quotes next to them. Often the fix is a missing proof point or an unclear line, not a missing feature. Those are product marketing fixes.

## Automating the log

Workspace Studio has a starter that runs when a meeting transcript is ready, and steps that can ask Gemini and add rows to a sheet. That could write the Objections tab for you. Google’s starter guide (https://support.google.com/workspace-studio/answer/16765661) notes that this starter fires on the transcript, not on Gemini’s notes, so whether a flow sees the slide screenshots is something to test. We haven’t yet.

## What we have tested

- **Checked in Sheets:** the COUNTIFS summary formula.
- **Not yet checked by us:** screenshot capture itself. It was rolling out when we wrote this; availability depends on your Workspace edition and admin settings.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Certify reps on the new message with a Forms quiz

*Aug 4, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

A launch isn't landed until the people selling it can say it. Build a short quiz from the messaging, score it in Sheets, and follow up with whoever missed.

## TL;DR
- Since July 30, Help me create in Google Forms can generate a quiz, with correct answers, from a prompt and files.
- The best wrong answers are your own retired lines. They are plausible because you used to say them.
- Score in Sheets, set a pass mark, and follow up one to one.
- Keep it to ten questions. It checks recall of the message, not product knowledge.

## A message nobody can repeat isn't launched

Product marketing ships the new positioning, the deck, the one-pager. Two weeks later a rep describes the product the old way on a call. The assets changed. The words in people’s mouths didn’t.
A ten-question quiz after the enablement session tells you who has the new message and who needs a second pass. Google Forms has done quizzes for years. What changed is how fast you can build one.

## Route 1: let Gemini draft the quiz

On July 30, Google announced that Help me create in Google Forms now generates quizzes (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/use-gemini-in-google-forms-to-quickly-create-a-new-quiz.html). You describe the quiz in a prompt and point it at files, including PDFs. Gemini drafts the questions, sets quiz settings and marks the correct answers.

    Create a 10-question multiple choice quiz for account executives on our new SSO messaging.
    Use only the approved lines in the attached messaging doc as correct answers.
    Each question gets three wrong answers that sound plausible. Do not invent product facts.

Read every question before you send it. Gemini decides what to ask, and it may test a detail that doesn’t matter. Delete those. Check every correct answer against the messaging doc word for word.
Availability per Google’s post: Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, Education Plus.

## Route 2: build it from the messaging sheet

If your messages already live in a sheet, a script gives you exact control. The trick is the wrong answers. Generic distractors are easy to spot. Your **retired lines** are not: they are what the team said last quarter, and they are what a rep will say if the new message didn’t stick.

[Figure: Approved line becomes the correct answer. Retired lines become the wrong ones.]

Add a Question column and up to three Retired columns to the Messages tab. Then, in the sheet, open **Extensions › Apps Script** and paste:

    function buildMessagingQuiz() {
      const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActive().getSheetByName('Messages');
      const rows = sheet.getDataRange().getValues().slice(1);   // Key, Question, Approved line, Retired 1, Retired 2, Retired 3
      const form = FormApp.create('Messaging check: ' + new Date().toDateString());
      form.setIsQuiz(true);
      rows.filter(r => r[1] && r[2]).forEach(r => {
        const item = form.addMultipleChoiceItem();
        const options = [item.createChoice(r[2], true)]
          .concat(r.slice(3, 6).filter(String).map(t => item.createChoice(t, false)));
        item.setTitle(r[1]).setChoices(shuffle(options)).setPoints(1).setRequired(true);
      });
      form.setDestination(FormApp.DestinationType.SPREADSHEET, SpreadsheetApp.getActive().getId());
      Logger.log(form.getPublishedUrl());
    }
    
    function shuffle(a) {
      for (let i = a.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1)); [a[i], a[j]] = [a[j], a[i]]; }
      return a;
    }

Run `buildMessagingQuiz`. It creates a quiz form, one question per row, with the approved line marked correct and the options shuffled, and sends responses to a new tab in the same spreadsheet. The FormApp reference (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/forms) covers every call it uses.

## Score it and follow up

[Figure: Responses land in the sheet with a score. Mockup.]

- **Pass mark:** 8 of 10 is a reasonable start. Add a column: `=IF(C2>=8,"Pass","Follow up")`.
- **Look at the misses by question,** not only by person. If half the team picks the same retired line, the message is the problem, not the reps.
- **Follow up one to one.** A short call beats a public leaderboard.
- **Re-run after a change.** When a line changes, it moves to a Retired column and becomes a wrong answer in the next quiz.

## What we have tested

- **Not yet run by us:** the script above. It is written against the FormApp reference. Run it on a copy of your sheet first.
- **Not yet tried by us:** quiz generation with Help me create. Our account did not have it when we wrote this.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Localize a one-pager without breaking the layout

*Jul 31, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Translations run long. Give every slot a budget per language, draft in Sheets, and catch the overflow before it reaches the page.

## TL;DR
- Translated copy is a layout problem first. German and French lines often run longer than English; Japanese is shorter in characters but wider per character.
- Keep one row per slot in Sheets and one column per language, each with its own character budget.
- Draft with the Sheets AI function. Fill with Gemini now works in 11 more languages. A native speaker approves.
- Flag anything over budget in the sheet. Fix length there, never by shrinking type on the page.

## The page breaks before the translation does

A one-pager is built around its English copy. The headline box is sized for eight words. The three benefit columns are sized for two short lines each. Then the German version arrives and every box overflows.
You can fix it slide by slide, file by file, every launch. Or you can treat length as data and catch it before it reaches a page. The second way takes one sheet.

## One row per slot, one column per language

Every text box on the page is a slot with a key: `headline`, `subhead`, `benefit_1_title`. The sheet has one row per key. Each language gets a copy column and a budget column.

[Figure: One row per slot. The German headline is 11 characters over. Mockup.]

- **Key:** the slot name. It never changes between languages.
- **Source line:** the approved English line.
- **Budget per language:** the most characters that slot can hold in that language, at that size, in that font. Set it by filling the box until it looks full, then counting.
- **Fits:** `=IF(LEN(D2)<=E2,"OK","Over by "&(LEN(D2)-E2))`

Budgets differ by language for two reasons. Some languages need more letters to say the same thing. And a character count is a stand-in for width: a Japanese character takes far more room than a Latin *i*. Measure each language in its own font.

## Draft the translation in the sheet

Google announced on July 7 that Fill with Gemini in Sheets works in 11 more languages (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/fill-with-gemini-in-sheets-now-available-in-11-additional-languages.html). Fill with Gemini runs on the AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199), so you can write the budget into the prompt:

    =AI("Translate this product marketing line into German. Keep it under "&E2&" characters. Plain, specific, no exclamation marks.", B2)

Three rules keep this safe:

- **A draft is a draft.** A native speaker who knows the product approves every line. Machine drafts miss product terms and register.
- **Keep a glossary tab.** Product names, feature names and terms you never translate. Paste the relevant terms into the prompt.
- **Keep draft and approved separate.** A formula can recalculate. An approved line must not. Paste approved lines as values.

## Catch overflow in the sheet, not on the page

[Figure: One headline, four languages, one box. Budgets are set per language.]

When a line is over budget, shorten the line. Do not shrink the font for one language. A German headline set smaller than the English one breaks the type system you built for every other asset, and readers notice.
Some fixes that work:

- **Write a shorter source line.** If three languages run over, the English line is too long for the layout.
- **Allow a two-line headline** in the layout, and budget for two lines in every language.
- **Split long compounds** with your translator, or choose a shorter term from the glossary.

## Fonts per language

Your brand font may not cover every script. Overpass, our headline font, has no Japanese glyphs. Pick a fallback per language and record it in the sheet, so everyone uses the same one. Google Fonts has Noto families for most scripts. Re-measure budgets in the fallback font.
Check letter spacing too. A tracked-out all-caps eyebrow in English can look wrong in a script with no capitals. Set tracking per language.

## One file per language

- Make a copy of the finished English file for each language. Keep page size, layout and slot names identical.
- Name files the same way: `One-pager - Relay - de-DE`.
- Paste approved lines slot by slot. If you tag text boxes with their key in the alt text title, a script can do this for every language at once.
- Look at every page after the copy lands. A count is an estimate; line breaks still surprise.

Logos and icons should not change between languages. Keep them as vectors so one file serves every version: see how to add a logo to Google Slides as an editable SVG (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides).

## What we have tested

- **Checked in Sheets:** the LEN-based fit formula.
- **Not checked by us:** translation quality from the AI function in each of the 11 new languages. Google’s post lists them; treat every draft as a draft.

*Update, Nov 2026:* the slot-and-sync approach mentioned above is now written up in full in Update Google Slides collateral from one messaging sheet with Gemini (https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini).
The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# What's new in SVG to Slides

## 1.4.0 (November 2026)

- Colour picker in the toolbar (Option+Shift+F for fill, Option+Shift+L for stroke): spectrum, hue and opacity sliders, eyedropper, hex field, the slide's colours and recent ones. With text highlighted it sets the colour of those words only. Colour changes are made on the object itself, so animation and links stay.
- Gradient builder: linear and radial, stops on a bar, an angle dial, a start point for radial. Results are native Slides gradients.
- Replace a colour: with nothing selected, pick a colour in use and what it becomes. Changes fills, strokes, gradient stops and text, inside groups too. "All slides" lists the deck's colours and runs across every slide; one Cmd+Z undoes it.
- Live preview: the slide shows the colour, opacity, gradient or stroke width while the panel is open.
- Mask image with shape (Option+Shift+K) keeps the shape on top as an unfilled outline, grouped with the masked picture. Double-click the group, or press Mask again, to move or resize the picture under its mask.
- SVG import: linear and radial gradients arrive as Slides gradients; opacity, fill-opacity and stroke-opacity come across.
- From 1.3.1: icon sets drawn with strokes (Lucide, Feather, Heroicons outline, Tabler) import as shapes.
- Limits: a gradient on a shape with mixed text styles replaces the shape (animation lost); a fill on a whole mask group is refused; stroke widths outside Slides' presets replace the shape.
- Permissions unchanged: access to Google Slides pages, where the tools run, and storage.

## 1.3.0 (November 2026)

- One toolbar at the left of the slide canvas (Option+Backslash): Layers, Edit Shape, Pen, command palette, Arrange, Align, Combine, Group, Outline, fill and stroke. Tooltips show shortcuts.
- Pen (Option+Shift+P): click for corners, drag for curves (Option breaks handles, Shift constrains to 45 degrees), click the first point to close, Enter or Esc to leave open, Delete removes the last point. New paths start as a 2 px dark stroke with no fill. Done adds them in one undo step.
- Snapping in the editor: points, the lines through them, slide edges and centre (pink guides), whole pixels, and a grid of any size (Cmd+' toggles). Hold Cmd to ignore.
- Exact strokes: weight field in px with Option-drag scrubbing (Shift x10), stroke inside/centre/outside, typed width, height, rotation and corner radius in Edit Shape; Edit Shape's box scales, stretches, rotates and skews.
- Outline text (Option+Cmd+T, restores on the same computer) and outline stroke (Option+Cmd+O).
- Mask image with shape (Option+Shift+K): any shape, group or outlined text over a picture. The picture keeps its exact position and size. Rotated images not yet supported.
- Combine: union, subtract, intersect, exclude, on the slide or in Edit Shape. One-press undo/redo for multi-step changes.
- Align and distribute are instant and keep images intact; a single object, image included, aligns to the slide edges.
- Layers (Option+1): nested groups fold open, Cmd-click selects inside groups, rename, hide, restack, zoom to tiny objects. Theme objects are greyed with an M; a second click opens the theme builder on them (Option+Shift+M), where one change updates every slide using that layout or master.
- Command palette (Cmd+Backslash): every command and shortcut, searchable.
- Paste SVG code: SVG markup on the clipboard pastes as native shapes.
- Small SVGs keep full detail when enlarged later.
- 92% smaller (installed 14 MB to 1.1 MB): the converter is JavaScript now. No server, and the permission for its address is gone; files never leave the browser. Permissions left: access to Google Slides pages, where the tools run, and storage.
- Fixes: layer tooltips, layer rename, false theme and too-small flags, align preview measurement.

## 1.2.0 (November 2026)

- Edit Shape: double-click a shape, then click Edit Shape. A vector editor opens on the slide at the shape's exact size and position. Drag points and curve handles, add or remove points, multi-select, undo, redo, zoom. Done updates the shape in place.
- Round corners: on shapes with corners, drag a circle inside a corner or type a pixel radius. The whole shape or several shapes round every corner together; selected points round only those corners.
- Layers stay put: shapes above the one you're editing stay visible, and Done returns each shape to its place in the stack.
- Works on Slides' own shapes, lines, text boxes and WordArt by converting them to custom shapes first. Adjustment handles, connection points, automatic 3D shading and editable WordArt text don't carry over. Text inside a shape stays editable. Cancel restores the original.
- Click to insert: drop an SVG and click where it goes. It lands as native shapes with nothing to paste. Falls back to Cmd/Ctrl+V if Slides refuses the insert.
- Straight-line SVG shapes land as Slides polylines, so Slides' own Edit points works on them.
- Placement and the editor measure the slide you have open.
- Adds the Chrome "storage" permission, used only to show the update note once. Still no access to your Google account.

## 1.0.1 (July 2026)
Removed an unused permission flagged in Chrome Web Store review.

## 1.0.0 (July 2026)
First release: drag SVG files onto a Google Slides tab and they land as native, editable shapes.

Get it: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi

# About SVG to Slides

SVG to Slides turns SVG files into native, editable shapes inside Google Slides. Every path becomes its own shape: select it, recolour it with the standard fill picker, resize it without losing quality.

- Three ways in: Chrome extension (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi), web uploader (https://svgslid.es/convert), Google Slides add-on (https://svgslid.es/addon).
- The extension asks for no access to your Google account.
- Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

## Why it exists
Slides has no way to import an SVG; pasted SVGs flatten into images. Where there should be crisp icons and logos, there are crunchy PNGs.

## How it works
SVG to Slides writes Google Slides' own clipboard shape format from your SVG's paths and hands it to Slides, which treats the result as native shapes. The extension converts inside your browser. Since 1.2 it also edits shapes: double-click any shape to move its points and curves. Version 1.3 adds a toolbar with a pen, outline text, image masks, union and subtract, a layers panel and a command palette (https://svgslid.es/whats-new).

## Who builds it
Joe Gelman, independently. Contact: joe@glmn.co


---

# What SVG to Slides does

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Google Slides has no SVG import. An SVG placed on a slide is flattened into a picture. SVG to Slides converts each path of the SVG into a native Slides shape, so the result can be selected, recoloured, resized and reshaped like a shape drawn in Slides.

## The three products

| Product | How you use it | Where conversion runs | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chrome extension** | Drag .svg files onto an open Slides tab and click where they go. | In your browser. | Native shapes on the slide you have open. See [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md). |
| **Web Uploader** | Upload files on a web page. No install. | On the svgslid.es server. | A Google Drive link to a file with one slide per SVG. See [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). |
| **Workspace Add-on** | Pick files in a dialog inside Slides, copy, paste. | On the svgslid.es server. | Native shapes on the current slide. See [Workspace Add-on](https://svgslid.es/docs/add-on.md). |

The shapes are ordinary Slides objects. They take the standard fill picker, resize without loss of quality, work in themes, and work in Google Drawings.

## What the extension adds on the slide

From version 1.2.0 the extension edits shapes as well as importing them. Version 1.3.0 adds a toolbar and the tools below.

| Tool | What it is for | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| Edit Shape | Move the points and curves of any shape. | [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md) |
| Round corners | Drag or type a corner radius. | [Rounding corners](https://svgslid.es/docs/round-corners.md) |
| Pen | Draw new shapes point by point. | [Drawing with the pen](https://svgslid.es/docs/pen.md) |
| Snapping | Snap points to other points, pixels or a grid. | [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md) |
| Mask | Cut a picture to any shape. | [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md) |
| Combine | Union, subtract, intersect, exclude. | [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md) |
| Align and distribute | Instant, images included. | [Aligning and distributing](https://svgslid.es/docs/align-distribute.md) |
| Layers | List, rename, hide and restack objects. | [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md) |
| Outline | Turn strokes and text into shapes. | [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md) |
| Command palette | Every command and its shortcut. | [The command palette](https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette.md) |

## Price and account

SVG to Slides is free. There is no account, no daily cap and no paid tier. The extension asks for no access to your Google account. See [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md).

## What does not convert

Some SVG features have no Slides equivalent or are not handled yet. Clip paths, masks, pattern fills, filters and transparency are examples. The tested list is in [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md).

# Installing and updating the extension

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0.

The extension installs from the Chrome Web Store and needs no account. It runs only on Google Slides editor pages. Chrome updates it automatically.

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Browser | Google Chrome on a desktop computer. |
| Page | A Google Slides presentation open for editing. The extension does not run on other pages. |
| Account | None. |
| Chrome permissions | Version 1.3.0: storage. Earlier versions: see [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#by-version). |

**To install the extension**

1. Open [svgslid.es/chrome](https://svgslid.es/chrome). It leads to the SVG to Slides page in the Chrome Web Store.
2. Click **Add to Chrome**.
3. Open a Google Slides presentation. If one was already open, reload its tab.

In version 1.3.0 a round button appears at the left edge of the slide canvas. That button is the toolbar, closed. See [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md).

## Checking your version

**To see which version is installed**

1. In Chrome's address bar, type `chrome://extensions` and press Enter.
2. Find **SVG to Slides**. The version number is shown beside the name.

Each topic in this library states the versions it applies to. If a tool described here is missing, compare your version with the topic's box.

## How updates arrive

Chrome updates extensions on its own, usually within a few hours of a new version being published in the Chrome Web Store. You do not need to do anything.

The first time you open Slides after an update, a short note in the corner of the page names what changed and links to the release post. It appears once. New installations do not see it.

> **Note:** An update can change the permissions the extension holds. Version 1.3.0 removed one, and version 1.4.0 changes none. See [Version 1.3.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-3-0.md#packaging).

## See also

- [Quick start](https://svgslid.es/docs/quick-start.md)
- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Version history](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes.md)
- [HOWTO: Find which version of the extension is installed](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/which-version.md)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/install (SVG to Slides Documentation, Getting Started). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Quick start: your first SVG

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later.

Drag an .svg file onto a slide, click where it goes, and it lands as native shapes. This topic walks through the first insert and the three things most people do next.

**To put an SVG on a slide**

1. Open your presentation in Google Chrome with the extension installed.
2. Drag an .svg file from a folder on your computer onto the slide. A faint preview follows the pointer with the label **Click to Place**.
3. Click where the graphic should go. It lands there as shapes, selected.

![A Google Slides slide with a faint palm icon under the pointer and a pill reading Click to Place](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/insert-click-to-place.jpg)
Figure 1. The file has been dropped. The preview follows the pointer until you click.

## What to do next

| To do this | Do this |
|---|---|
| Change a colour | Select a shape and use Slides' fill picker. Each path of the SVG is its own shape, so parts recolour separately. |
| Resize | Drag a selection handle. The shapes are vectors, so edges stay sharp at any size. |
| Work on one part | Shapes from one file arrive grouped. Double-click to reach a shape inside the group. In version 1.3.0 you can also hold Command and click it. See [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md#direct-select). |
| Change the outline | Double-click a shape and click **Edit Shape**. See [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md). |
| Open the tools | In version 1.3.0, click the round button at the left of the slide, or press Option+\. See [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md). |

> **Tip:** To bring in many files, select up to 25 and drag them together. See [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#several).

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md)
- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [Guide: Recolor SVGs in Google Slides](https://svgslid.es/guides/recolor-svg-in-google-slides)

# Document conventions

Applies to: All SVG to Slides documentation.

This library uses a small set of conventions for keys, interface names, versions and notes. Keys are given for Mac. The Windows key follows a fixed rule.

## Keys

Keys are printed in capitals and joined with a plus sign. Option+Shift+P means hold OPTION and SHIFT and press P. A phrase such as "Command-click" means hold the key and click.

Key combinations are given for Mac. On Windows, use the key in the second column. Point at any key combination in a topic to see the Windows form.

| Mac | Windows |
|---|---|
| Command | Ctrl |
| Option | Alt |
| Shift | Shift |
| Delete | Backspace |
| Command+Control+K | Ctrl+Alt+K |

The full list, with both columns, is in [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md).

## Typography

| Convention | Used for |
|---|---|
| **Bold** | Names you see on screen: buttons, menus, panel titles. |
| *Italic* | A value you supply. |
| `Monospace` | File names, addresses, SVG code and text you type. |
| CAPITALS in a box | Keys. |

Spelling follows the product: colour, centre.

## Versions

Each topic opens with a box headed "The information in this topic applies to". If the box names a version "and later", the tool is not present in versions before it. To find your version, see [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#check-version).

## Procedures

A procedure starts with a line that begins "To", followed by numbered steps. Do the steps in order. A step that has a result says what you should see.

## Notes

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Note | Information that qualifies the text around it. |
| Tip | A faster or easier way. |
| Important | Something that affects the result if you miss it. |
| Caution | A step that loses work or cannot be reversed. |

## Figures

Screen pictures show the extension's own interface running over a sample deck, the Vacay.com pitch deck. Numbered yellow markers on a figure match the numbered list under it.

Figures labelled *Illustration* are frames from the release animations. They show the result on the slide and draw the toolbar in simplified form.

## Knowledge Base articles

Knowledge Base articles are numbered Q100101 and up. The first word of the title gives the kind of article.

| Prefix | Kind of article |
|---|---|
| PRB | A problem and its cause. The behaviour may be by design. |
| FIX | A problem that a later version corrects. |
| INFO | Background on how something behaves. |
| HOWTO | A procedure. |

## See also

- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
- [All articles](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb.md)
- [Glossary](https://svgslid.es/docs/glossary.md)
- [Index](https://svgslid.es/docs/a-z-index.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/conventions (SVG to Slides Documentation, Getting Started). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Inserting SVG files

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0. Click to place: version 1.2.0 and later. Pasting SVG code: version 1.3.0 and later. Gradients and transparency: version 1.4.0..

Drag one or more .svg files from your computer onto an open Google Slides tab, then click where they go. Every path lands as its own native shape. Paths from one file arrive as a group.

**To insert an SVG file**

1. Open the presentation in Google Chrome.
2. Drag the .svg file from a folder or the desktop onto the slide. A faint preview of the file follows the pointer, with a green plus badge and the label **Click to Place**.
3. Click the point where the graphic should be centred.

The shapes appear at that point, selected. Nothing needs pasting.

![A slide with a faint palm icon under the pointer, a green plus badge and a grey pill reading Click to Place](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/insert-click-to-place.jpg)
Figure 1. After the drop. The preview follows the pointer until you click.

## Size and position

The graphic is fitted to about a fifth of the slide and centred on the point you click. Resize it afterwards with Slides' selection handles.

From version 1.3.0 a graphic keeps all of its detail however small it lands, so it can be enlarged later without loss. See [Point precision](https://svgslid.es/docs/point-precision.md).

## Several files at once

Select up to 25 .svg files and drag them together. They land on the current slide in a grid, each file as its own group.

If the drop holds more than 25 .svg files, nothing is inserted and a message says so. Use the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md) for larger batches. See [PRB: Nothing is inserted when more than 25 files are dropped](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/more-than-25-files.md).

## Pasting SVG code

In version 1.3.0, SVG markup copied as text can be pasted onto the slide. Copy the code, click the slide and press Command+V. The same preview appears, and you click to place it.

## Cancelling

Press Esc before you click. The preview disappears and nothing is inserted.

## Files that are not SVG

A drop that holds no .svg file is left to Slides, which handles it as it always does.

## If the extension asks you to press COMMAND+V

The extension hands the shapes to Slides the way a paste does. If Slides does not accept them, the extension shows a prompt to press Command+V. Press it and the shapes land. See [INFO: The extension asks you to press COMMAND+V](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/press-command-v-prompt.md).

> **Note:** In versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 every insert ended with Command+V. The click has inserted directly since version 1.2.0.

## What converts

Paths, basic shapes, arcs, transforms and cut-outs convert. Strokes, including outline icon sets, become filled shapes. Since version 1.4.0 linear and radial gradients arrive as Slides gradients, and `opacity`, `fill-opacity` and `stroke-opacity` are kept. In earlier versions a gradient arrives as its first colour. Text, masks, patterns and filters do not convert in the extension. The full table is in [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md).

## See also

- [Quick start](https://svgslid.es/docs/quick-start.md)
- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)

# The toolbar

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

The toolbar sits at the left edge of the slide canvas. Closed, it is one round button. Click the button or press Option+\ to open it. It holds every tool the extension adds to Slides.

## The toolbar, closed

![The left edge of a Google Slides canvas with one round yellow SVG button beside the slide](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/toolbar-closed.jpg)
Figure 1. The toolbar when closed.
1. The svgslid.es button. Click it, or press Option+\, to open the toolbar.

The toolbar starts closed. Once you open or close it, the extension remembers the state on this computer.

## The toolbar, open

![The open toolbar: a two-column strip of icon buttons at the left of the slide, with numbered markers](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/toolbar-open.jpg)
Figure 2. The toolbar when open, with the logo selected. Buttons that do not apply to the selection are dimmed.
1. svgslid.es button. Closes the toolbar.
2. **Layers**. Opens the [Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md).
3. **Edit Shape**. Opens the [point editor](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md) on the selection.
4. **Pen**. [Draws a new shape](https://svgslid.es/docs/pen.md).
5. **Commands**. Opens the [command palette](https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette.md).
6. **Arrange**. Bring forward, send backward, front, back.
7. **Align and distribute**. See [Aligning and distributing](https://svgslid.es/docs/align-distribute.md).
8. **Combine**. Union, subtract, intersect, exclude. See [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md).
9. **Group**, **Ungroup** and **Mask image with shape**. See [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md).
10. **Outline stroke** and **Outline text**. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md).
11. **Fill colour** and **Stroke colour**.
12. Stroke weight in pixels. Type a value. 0 means no stroke.
13. **Stroke position** and **Stroke on / off**. See [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md).

| Section | Buttons | Shortcuts |
|---|---|---|
| Top | svgslid.es button, Layers, Edit Shape, Pen, Commands | Option+\, Option+1, double-click, Option+Shift+P, Command+\ |
| Place | Arrange, Align and distribute | See [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#arrange) |
| Combine | Union, Subtract, Intersect, Exclude | Option+Shift+U, Option+Shift+S, Option+Shift+I, Option+Shift+E |
| Group | Group, Ungroup, Mask image with shape | Command+Option+G, Shift+Command+Option+G, Option+Shift+K |
| Outline | Outline stroke, Outline text | Option+Command+O, Option+Command+T |
| Paint | Fill colour, Stroke colour, weight, Stroke position, Stroke on / off | Option+Shift+F, Option+Shift+L, Option+Shift+[ and Option+Shift+], Option+Shift+/ |

## Tooltips

Point at any button, pop-out item or field to see its name and shortcut.

![The pointer over the Pen button with a dark tooltip reading Pen: draw a shape anywhere, Option Shift P](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/toolbar-tooltip.jpg)
Figure 3. A tooltip. Every control has one.

## Pop-out menus

Buttons with a small mark in the corner open a row of commands beside the toolbar. Arrange, Align and distribute, and Stroke position work this way.

![The Align and distribute button open, showing eight align and distribute buttons in a row, with a tooltip on Align centres horizontally](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/align-flyout.jpg)
Figure 4. The Align and distribute pop-out, with three objects selected.

## Dimmed buttons

A button is dimmed when its command does not apply to what is selected. Outline text, for example, is dimmed unless the selection has text. Clicking a dimmed command shows a short message that says what to select.

## Short screens

When the canvas is too short for the whole toolbar, the Combine buttons fold into one pop-out button, then the Outline buttons do the same.

## While a command runs

While the extension carries out a command the toolbar ignores clicks and the pointer shows the progress cursor. This lasts a moment.

## When the toolbar is hidden

The toolbar is hidden while Edit Shape is open, because the editor has its own toolbar in the same place. It is also hidden in full-screen view.

## See also

- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
- [Command reference](https://svgslid.es/docs/commands.md)
- [The command palette](https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette.md)
- [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Edit Shape: points and curves

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later. The box, exact values and the two-column editor toolbar: version 1.3.0 and later..

Edit Shape opens a vector editor on the slide at the shape's exact size and position. Drag points and curve handles, add or remove points, then click **Done**. The shape updates in place and returns to its place in the stack.

**To edit a shape's points**

1. Double-click the shape, then click **Edit Shape**. In version 1.3.0 you can also select the shape and click **Edit Shape** on the toolbar.
2. Drag a point to move it. Click a point to see its curve handles, and drag a handle to change the curve.
3. Click **Done**, or press Enter.

![The Edit Shape editor open on a palm tree icon. Every point of the outline is marked, a box with handles surrounds the shape, and the editor toolbar is at the left.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/edit-shape.jpg)
Figure 1. Edit Shape open on a palm icon, version 1.3.0. Round marks are smooth points and square marks are corner points.
1. **Select** tool. V
2. **Pen** tool. Adds and removes points, and draws. P
3. **Snapping**. See [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md).
4. The same command groups as the main toolbar: Arrange, Align, Combine, Group, Outline, fill and stroke.
5. Undo and redo, point by point.
6. Zoom. Click to return to 100%.
7. **Cancel**. Discards the edit.
8. **Done**. Applies the edit.
9. Size pill: width, height and rotate-by. On shapes with corners it also shows the corner radius.
10. The hint line names the keys for the current tool.

## Points and handles

| To do this | Do this |
|---|---|
| Move a point | Drag it. Hold Shift to keep to 45° steps. |
| Change a curve | Click the point, then drag one of its handles. |
| Move one handle only | Hold Option while dragging the handle. |
| Switch a point between smooth and corner | Double-click the point. |
| Add a point | Press P, then click the outline where the point should be. |
| Remove a point | Press P, then click the point. |
| Select several points | Shift-click each one, or drag a box around them. |
| Select every point of a shape | Click the shape. |
| Select all points | Command+A |
| Nudge | Arrow keys. Hold Shift for ten times the step. |
| Delete the selected points | Delete |
| Undo, redo | Command+Z, Shift+Command+Z |
| Zoom | Pinch, or Command+Plus and Command+Minus. Command+0 returns to 100%. |
| Pan | Hold Spacebar and drag, or scroll. |

![A palm tree outline with one point selected and its two curve handles extended, the pointer on a handle](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/edit-points-1-2.jpg)
Figure 2. A selected point and its two handles. Recorded in Google Slides with version 1.2.0, whose editor toolbar had one column.

## The box

In version 1.3.0 a box surrounds the selection inside the editor. Dragging it transforms the shape while its points stay editable.

| Drag | Result |
|---|---|
| A corner | Scale. Shift keeps the proportions. Option scales from the centre. |
| An edge | Stretch in one direction. Option stretches from the centre. |
| Command + an edge | Skew. Shift snaps to 15°. |
| Command + a corner, or just outside a corner | Rotate. Shift snaps to 15°. |

## Typing exact values

The pill under the shape holds the width and height in pixels, a rotate-by field and, on shapes with corners, the corner radius. Type a value and press Enter. Hold Option and drag across any number to change it by dragging. Add Shift for steps of ten.

## Commands inside the editor

The editor's toolbar repeats the command groups of the main toolbar. Inside the editor a command acts on the shapes that have selected points, or on every shape in the editor when no point is selected. Combine, group, ungroup, outline, fill and stroke are held in the editor and applied when you click **Done**.

## Done and Cancel

**Done** replaces the shape on the slide with the edited one, in the same place in the stack. Shapes above it stay visible while you edit, so you can line points up against them. In version 1.3.0 the whole session is one undo step. See [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md).

**Cancel** discards the edit. Esc clears the selection first. With nothing selected, Esc applies the edit the same as **Done**.

> **Important:** **Done** puts a new object in place of the original. Animations and links attached to the original do not carry over. A shape edited from inside a group comes back just above that group.

## What can be edited

Edit Shape opens directly on shapes inserted by SVG to Slides. On Slides' own shapes, lines, text boxes and WordArt it converts the object first. See [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md). Images, video and charts cannot be edited as shapes.

## See also

- [Rounding corners](https://svgslid.es/docs/round-corners.md)
- [Drawing with the pen](https://svgslid.es/docs/pen.md)
- [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md)
- [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md)
- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#editor)
- [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Rounding corners

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later.

In Edit Shape, shapes with corners show a small circle just inside each corner. Drag a circle toward the middle of the shape to round the corner, or type a radius in pixels.

**To round the corners of a shape**

1. Open the shape in Edit Shape. See [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md).
2. Drag one of the small circles inside a corner toward the middle of the shape. A pill under the shape shows the radius in pixels.
3. To set an exact radius, type a value in the pill and press Enter.
4. Click **Done**.

![Three cards on a slide in Edit Shape, each with rounded corners and a circle inside every corner. A pill under them reads 25 px, All corners.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/round-corners-1-2.jpg)
Figure 1. Three cards, twelve corners, one radius. Recorded in Google Slides with version 1.2.0.

## Which corners change

| Selection in the editor | Corners that round |
|---|---|
| The whole shape, or nothing | Every corner of the shape. |
| Several shapes | Every corner of every shape, together. |
| One point or a few points | Those corners only. |

Hold Shift while dragging to change the radius in steps of 10 pixels.

## Several shapes at once

**To give several shapes the same radius**

1. Select the shapes on the slide.
2. Open Edit Shape.
3. Type the radius in the pill and press Enter.
4. Click **Done**.

## See also

- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#exact-values)
- [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/round-corners (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Drawing with the pen

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

The pen draws new shapes point by point, anywhere on the slide. Press Option+Shift+P or click **Pen** on the toolbar. Click for a corner, drag for a curve, and click the first point to close the shape.

**To draw a shape**

1. With nothing selected, press Option+Shift+P or click **Pen** on the toolbar. An empty editor opens over the slide.
2. Click to place a corner point. To make a curve, press, drag and release.
3. Click the first point to close the shape. A ring appears on the first point when the pointer is over it. To leave the path open, press Enter or Esc.
4. Click **Done**. The new shapes are placed on the slide, on top.

![The pen editor over a slide with a grid showing. A speech-bubble outline is half drawn, with a dashed line from the last point to the pointer and a pink mark where it will snap.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/pen-drawing.jpg)
Figure 1. Seven points placed with the grid on. The dashed segment follows the pointer and the pink mark shows where the next point will snap.

## Pen keys

| To do this | Do this |
|---|---|
| Place a corner point | Click. |
| Place a smooth point | Press, drag, release. |
| Make a sharp turn after a curve | Hold Option while dragging to break the handles. |
| Keep to 45° steps | Hold Shift. |
| Close the shape | Click the first point. |
| Leave the path open | Enter or Esc |
| Remove the last point | Delete |
| Undo one point | Command+Z |
| Carry on an open path | Click its end point. |
| Add a point to a path | Click a segment. |
| Remove a point from a path | Click the point. |
| Switch to the Select tool | V |

## What you get

Each path becomes a new shape. The first shape you draw has a 2 pixel dark stroke and no fill. Each later shape starts with the paint of the last one drawn. Set a fill or stroke from the editor's toolbar before you click **Done**, or afterwards on the slide.

**Done** places all the new shapes in one undo step.

## Pen with shapes selected

If shapes are selected when you press Option+Shift+P, the editor opens on those shapes and the pen can both edit them and draw new ones beside them.

## Limits

The pen draws point by point. There is no freehand mode.

## See also

- [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md)
- [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#editor)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/pen (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Snapping

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Snapping pulls pen points and dragged points onto other points, the slide's edges and centre, whole pixels, or a grid. The magnet button in the editor's toolbar sets it. Points and pixels are on to start.

![The Snapping pop-out beside the editor toolbar with three toggle buttons and a grid size field reading 10 px](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/snapping-menu.jpg)
Figure 1. The Snapping pop-out.
1. **Snap to points**, the lines through them, and the slide's edges and centre.
2. **Snap to whole pixels**.
3. **Snap to the grid**. Turning it on shows the grid.
4. Grid size in pixels.

## Snap to points

A point being placed or dragged snaps to other points, to the horizontal and vertical lines through them, and to the slide's edges and centre. Pink guides and a pink cross show what caught it. A point wins over the grid and pixels when it is within 6 screen pixels.

## Snap to whole pixels

Positions are rounded to whole pixels.

## Snap to the grid

The grid starts at the slide's top-left corner. The size is 10 pixels to start. Type a size in the field to change it, which also turns the grid on. Press Command+' to show or hide the grid. The grid is not drawn when its lines would be less than 6 pixels apart on screen.

## What snaps

- Pen points and their handles, and the dashed preview segment.
- Dragged points. The point you grab snaps and the rest of the selection follows.
- Dragged handles.

## Turning snapping off for one move

Hold Command while placing or dragging to ignore snapping. Shift still keeps a move to 45° steps.

## Where the settings are kept

Snapping settings are kept on this computer. They are not part of the presentation.

## See also

- [Drawing with the pen](https://svgslid.es/docs/pen.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#editor)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#storage)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Masking an image with a shape

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later. The shape kept on top, and moving the picture under its mask: version 1.4.0..

Put a shape over a picture, select both, and press Option+Shift+K. The shape cuts out the picture under it and stays on top as an outline. Any shape or group of shapes can be the mask. Double-click the result to move or resize the picture under its mask.

**To mask an image with a shape**

1. Place the shape over the picture, where the picture should show through.
2. Select the picture and the shape. Click one, then Shift-click the other.
3. Press Option+Shift+K, or click **Mask image with shape** in the Group section of the toolbar.

The picture is cut to the shape. It is neither stretched nor re-cropped. The change is one undo step.

![Two views of a slide. On the left a yellow arch sits over a beach photograph. On the right the photograph shows only inside the arch.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/mask-before-after.jpg)
Figure 1. Before and after. An arch over a photograph, then the photograph cut to the arch. *Illustration.*

## What you get

In version 1.4.0 the result is a group of two objects:

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| The masked picture | The picture, cut to the shape. It takes the place in the stack of whichever of the two objects was higher. |
| The shape | The shape you used, on top of the picture, with its fill set to none. Its stroke stays, so it reads as an outline. |

A mask made of several shapes (a group, or outlined text) has each of its shapes emptied the same way.

> **Note:** In version 1.3.0 the shape is used up and only the masked picture remains.

## Moving the picture under its mask

**To move or resize the picture under its mask**

1. Double-click the mask group, or select it and press Option+Shift+K again. The whole picture shows, faded where the mask hides it, with a bar under the mask.
2. Drag the picture to move it. Drag a corner to resize it. The arrow keys nudge it.
3. To set an exact size, type a percentage in the **Picture** field. **Fit** sizes the picture to cover the mask.
4. Press Enter or click the tick to keep the change. Press Esc or click the cross to cancel.

The mask and the outline shape stay where they are. Only the picture moves. The change is one undo step.

![A photograph masked by an arch on a slide. The whole photograph shows faded around the arch, with a dashed frame, corner handles, and a dark bar under the arch holding a Picture percentage field, Fit, a cross and a tick.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/mask-adjust.jpg)
Figure 2. Adjusting the picture. The part the mask hides is shown faded. *Illustration.*

## Changing the outline afterwards

Select the masked picture inside the group (click the group, then click the picture) and open it in [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md). The picture holds still while the outline changes. The editor draws the shape grey while you edit, and the picture returns when you click **Done**.

The outline shape on top is a separate object. It does not follow the edit. Reshape it the same way, or delete it.

## Colour on a mask group

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Stroke colour or weight on the group | Applied to the shape. The picture is left alone. |
| Fill on the group | Refused, because a fill would cover the picture. Select the shape inside the group to fill it on its own. |

## Requirements and limits

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| The mask is a group of shapes | Works. The group counts as one mask. |
| The mask is text | Outline the text first with Option+Command+T. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md). |
| The image is rotated | Not supported yet. Straighten the image first. |
| The shape is very thin | The extension reports that the shape is too thin to mask with. |
| More or fewer than two objects are selected | Select one image and one shape, or one image and one group. |

See [PRB: Mask image with shape shows a message and does not mask](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/cannot-mask-image.md) for the messages and what each one means.

## See also

- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md)
- [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md)
- [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md)
- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [PRB: Mask image with shape shows a message and does not mask](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/cannot-mask-image.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Combining shapes

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Union, Subtract, Intersect and Exclude make one shape from two or more. They work on the slide and inside Edit Shape, and each is one undo step.

## The four commands

| Command | Result | Shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| **Union** | One shape covering everything the selected shapes cover. | Option+Shift+U |
| **Subtract** | The bottom shape with the shapes above it cut out. | Option+Shift+S |
| **Intersect** | Only the area where the shapes overlap. | Option+Shift+I |
| **Exclude** | Everything except the area where the shapes overlap. | Option+Shift+E |

**To combine shapes**

1. Select two or more shapes.
2. Click the command in the Combine section of the toolbar, or press its shortcut.

![Two views of a slide. On the left, three overlapping circles and a rounded bar. On the right, a single cloud shape.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/combine-before-after.jpg)
Figure 1. Before and after Union. Four shapes become one cloud. *Illustration.*

Press Command+Z once to split them again. See [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md).

## Inside Edit Shape

The same four buttons are on the editor's toolbar. There they act on the shapes that have selected points, or on every shape in the editor, and the result is applied when you click **Done**.

## Limits

- Gradients, pattern fills, transparency and shadows are not carried into the result.
- Images, video and charts cannot be combined.
- The shapes need a fill or an outline.
- Intersect needs shapes that overlap. If a command would leave nothing, the extension says so and changes nothing.

## See also

- [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Aligning and distributing

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

The align and distribute commands move objects in one step, straight to the result, and leave images intact. One object on its own, an image included, aligns to the slide's edges.

## Commands

| Command | Shortcut | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Align left | Option+A | One object or more |
| Align centres horizontally | Option+H | One object or more |
| Align right | Option+D | One object or more |
| Align top | Option+W | One object or more |
| Align middles vertically | Option+V | One object or more |
| Align bottom | Option+S | One object or more |
| Distribute horizontal spacing | Option+Shift+H | Three objects or more |
| Distribute vertical spacing | Option+Shift+V | Three objects or more |

**To align objects**

1. Select the objects.
2. Click **Align and distribute** on the toolbar and choose a command, or press its shortcut.

![The Align and distribute pop-out with eight buttons and a tooltip reading Align centres horizontally, Option H](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/align-flyout.jpg)
Figure 1. The pop-out, with a title, a date and a logo selected.

With two or more objects selected, the objects align to each other.

## One object aligns to the slide

With one object selected, the align commands use the slide. Left, right, top and bottom move the object to that edge of the slide. Centre and middle centre it on the page.

This works for images. The extension places a 1 pixel helper at the corner of the slide it needs, runs Slides' own Align, and removes the helper, all in one undo step. Nothing extra is left in the presentation.

![Two views of the left half of a slide. A small photograph sits in the middle on the left view and in the bottom-left corner on the right view.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/align-edge-before-after.jpg)
Figure 2. A single photograph before and after Align left and Align bottom. *Illustration.*

## How the commands run

The extension runs Slides' own Align, Distribute and Center on page commands behind a still copy of the slide. You see the objects move once. Because the objects are moved by Slides and not deleted and pasted, images stay intact. See [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md).

## See also

- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md#pop-outs)
- [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md)
- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#align)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/align-distribute (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# The Layers panel

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Press Option+1 to list every object on the current slide, front first. Click a row to select the object. Drag rows to restack, double-click to rename, and use the eye to hide an object while you work.

![The Layers panel docked at the left of Google Slides, listing two text layers, a group named Vacay logo with two shapes inside, an image named Beach photo, and two greyed theme objects marked M](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/layers-panel.jpg)
Figure 1. The Layers panel on the cover slide of the sample deck.
1. Close. Slides' filmstrip returns.
2. A text layer. It is named by its words until you rename it.
3. A group. The arrow folds it open and closed.
4. The objects inside the group.
5. The eye hides an object in your view.
6. A theme object, greyed and marked **M**. See [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md).
7. The **Layers** button on the toolbar.
8. A reminder of the rules.

The panel docks over Slides' filmstrip and shows the slide you have open. Close the panel to get the filmstrip back.

## Working with rows

| To do this | Do this |
|---|---|
| Select an object | Click its row. This works for objects inside groups too. |
| Add to the selection | Shift-click a row. |
| Restack | Drag a row up or down. Only top-level rows can be dragged. |
| Rename | Double-click the name and type. Enter keeps the name. Esc cancels. Clicking elsewhere keeps it. |
| Open or close a group | Click the arrow beside it. Selecting an object inside a group opens the groups around it. |
| Hide or show | Click the eye. |

## Hiding

The eye hides an object in your view of the editor so that you can reach what is behind it. The object stays in the presentation. Other people still see it, and it still appears in the slideshow and in exports. Hiding lasts until you click the eye again or reload the page.

## Small objects

An object smaller than 6 pixels on screen is hard to click. The first click on its row says so. A second click within 5 seconds zooms in on the object and selects it.

## Selecting on the slide inside groups

Hold Command and click an object on the slide to select the innermost object under the pointer, however deep it is in groups. Shift+Command-click adds to the selection. While Command is held, an outline shows what a click would pick.

## What is kept on this computer

Layer names are kept on the computer you used. They are not saved in the presentation and do not appear for other people or on another computer. Hiding is not kept at all: it applies to the page you have open. See [PRB: Layer names are missing on another computer](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/layer-names-missing.md).

## See also

- [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md)
- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Aligning and distributing](https://svgslid.es/docs/align-distribute.md)
- [PRB: Layer names are missing on another computer](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/layer-names-missing.md)
- [INFO: An object in Layers is greyed and marked M](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/object-greyed-with-m.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/layers (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Theme objects and the theme builder

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Objects that come from the slide's layout or master are drawn on the slide but cannot be changed there. The Layers panel greys them and marks them **M**. A second click opens Slides' theme builder on the layout or master that holds the object.

## What a theme object is

A logo in the corner of every slide, a footer line, a background shape: these usually live on a layout or on the master, and Slides draws them on each slide that uses that layout. On the slide they look like any other object, but a click does not select them.

## How they are marked

In the [Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md), theme objects are listed at the bottom, greyed, with an **M** badge. With Command held over the slide, a theme object gets a dashed amber outline in place of the blue one.

**To edit a theme object**

1. Click its row in the Layers panel. A message explains that the object belongs to the theme, and the row turns amber.
2. Click the row again within 5 seconds. Slides' theme builder opens on the layout or master that holds the object, with the object selected.
3. Make the change.
4. Press Option+Shift+M to go back to the slide.

A Command-click on a theme object on the slide follows the same two steps.

## The theme builder shortcut

Option+Shift+M opens the theme builder from any slide and returns from it. It is the same view that Slides opens from **View › Theme builder**.

> **Note:** A change made in the theme builder affects every slide that uses that layout or master.

## See also

- [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md)
- [INFO: An object in Layers is greyed and marked M](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/object-greyed-with-m.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#anytime)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# Outlining strokes and text

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

**Outline stroke** turns lines and borders into filled shapes. **Outline text** turns text into shapes whose points you can edit. On the computer that outlined it, the same command puts the text back.

## Outline stroke

**To turn a stroke into a shape**

1. Select a shape or line that has a stroke.
2. Press Option+Command+O, or click **Outline stroke** on the toolbar.

The stroke becomes a filled shape in the stroke's colour, as wide as the stroke was. A shape that had both a fill and a stroke becomes two shapes: the fill, and the outline that was its stroke. Use it when a border has to be reshaped, combined or used as a mask like any other shape.

## Outline text

**To turn text into shapes**

1. Select the text box or the shape that holds the text.
2. Press Option+Command+T, or click **Outline text** on the toolbar.

The text becomes filled shapes in the form of its letters. A shape that held the text stays as it was, without the text. The letter shapes can then be reshaped in [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md), combined, or used as a mask.

## Restoring text

Select the outlined text and press Option+Command+T again, or choose **Restore outlined text** from the [The command palette](https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette.md). The original text returns as live text, at the place and size the outlines have now.

> **Important:** Text can be restored only on the computer that outlined it. The extension keeps the original text on that computer. The presentation does not hold it.

## Fonts

To outline text the extension needs the font's letter shapes.

| Font | Where the letter shapes come from |
|---|---|
| A Google font | The extension downloads the font from Google Fonts. The request names the font family, weight and style. It carries nothing from your presentation. |
| A font installed on your computer | Chrome asks for permission to read your fonts. Allow it to continue. |
| A system font that cannot be downloaded | The extension uses a font with the same letter widths and shows a note naming it. |

If no source works, the extension reports that it could not get the font. See [PRB: Outline text reports that it could not get the font](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/outline-text-font.md).

## Stroke position

**Stroke position** on the toolbar sets whether a closed shape's stroke sits inside the outline, centred on it, or outside it. Slides always centres a stroke, so the extension moves the outline by half the stroke weight to get the other two.

The extension remembers the original outline on this computer, so **Centre stroke** returns to it.

## Limits

- Gradients, pattern fills, transparency and shadows are not carried into outlined shapes.
- Images, video and charts cannot be outlined.
- Outlined-text memory and stroke-position memory are kept on the computer you used.

## See also

- [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md)
- [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md)
- [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md)
- [PRB: Outline text reports that it could not get the font](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/outline-text-font.md)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#network)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# Colour, gradients, stroke and exact values

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later. The colour panel, gradients, text colour, Replace a colour and live preview: version 1.4.0..

The Paint section of the toolbar opens a colour panel for the fill or the stroke of the selection, with opacity, an eyedropper and a gradient builder. With text highlighted it sets the colour of those words. With nothing selected it replaces one colour across the slide or the whole presentation. The slide shows each change while you pick.

## The colour panel

| Command | Shortcut | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Fill colour** | Option+Shift+F | Opens the colour panel on the fill of the selection. |
| **Stroke colour** | Option+Shift+L | Opens the colour panel on the stroke of the selection. |

The bar under each button shows the current colour of the selection.

| Part of the panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Solid**, **Linear**, **Radial**, **None** | The kind of fill or stroke. **None** removes it. |
| The square | Sets how strong and how bright the colour is. Drag in it. |
| The rainbow bar | Sets the hue. |
| The second bar, and the **%** field | Set the opacity. |
| The eyedropper | Picks a colour from anywhere on the screen. |
| **Hex** | Takes a colour typed as 3, 6 or 8 hex digits. Eight digits include the opacity. |
| **On this slide** | The colours the open slide already uses. Click one to take it. |
| **Recent** | The colours you used last. They are kept on this computer. |
| The cross and the tick | The cross puts the slide back as it was. The tick keeps the change. Enter is the tick and Esc is the cross. |

![The colour panel open beside the toolbar on a slide. It has a title, Solid, Linear, Radial and None tabs, a colour square, hue and opacity bars, Hex and percent fields, swatches of the slide's colours, and a cross and a tick. The selected card on the slide shows the colour being picked.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/colour-panel.jpg)
Figure 1. The colour panel on a fill. The card on the slide already shows the colour in the panel. *Illustration.*

The panel places itself beside the toolbar and stays inside the window.

> **Note:** In version 1.3.0 the two buttons open Slides' own fill and border colour menus. Those menus are still there in Slides' toolbar and can be used at any time.

## Gradients

**To fill a shape with a gradient**

1. Select the shape and press Option+Shift+F.
2. Click **Linear** or **Radial**. The shape takes a gradient that starts from its current colour.
3. Click a stop on the bar to select it, then set its colour in the square or the **Hex** field. Click an empty part of the bar to add a stop. Drag a stop along the bar to move it. **Remove stop** deletes the selected stop, and **Reverse** swaps the order.
4. For a linear gradient, turn the dial or type an angle. For a radial gradient, choose where it starts: the middle or a corner.
5. Click the tick.

![The colour panel in Linear mode. Under the tabs is a gradient bar with three stops, a Stop percent field, Remove stop and Reverse buttons, an angle dial with a degrees field, and buttons for 0, 45, 90 and 180 degrees. The card on the slide is filled with the gradient.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/gradient-builder.jpg)
Figure 2. The gradient builder with three stops. *Illustration.*

The result is a gradient of Slides' own kind. It can be edited later in this panel or in Slides' own fill menu.

> **Note:** Slides does not keep a separate opacity for each stop. The opacity applies to the whole fill.

## Text colour

With a stretch of text highlighted in a text box, **Fill colour** opens the panel as **Text colour**. The colour applies to the highlighted words only, and the highlight stays. Text takes a solid colour, with no opacity.

## Replacing a colour

**To change one colour everywhere it is used**

1. Click an empty part of the slide so that nothing is selected.
2. Press Option+Shift+F. The panel opens as **Replace a colour**.
3. Click the colour to change in the list, or pick it from the slide with the eyedropper.
4. Set the new colour. The slide shows it in every place the old colour is used.
5. To change it on every slide, tick **All slides**. The list then shows the colours of the whole presentation.
6. Click the tick.

Fills, strokes, gradient stops and text are changed, inside groups too. A run across all slides shows a progress bar and is undone with one press of Command+Z.

![The panel titled Replace a colour, with the old colour and the new colour as two chips joined by an arrow, an All slides box, and the slide's colours listed. The card on the slide shows the new colour.](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/replace-colour.jpg)
Figure 3. Replace a colour. The old and the new colour are at the top of the panel. *Illustration.*

> **Note:** The colours of other slides are read from the filmstrip. In a long presentation, slides far down the filmstrip may not be listed until you scroll to them.

## Live preview

While the panel is open, the slide shows the colour, opacity, gradient or text colour in hand, and the stroke weight as you type or drag it. Nothing is changed in the presentation until you click the tick. The cross puts the slide back.

## How a colour change is applied

| Change | How it is made | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| Solid colour, fill opacity, text colour | Through Slides' own custom colour dialog. | The object, with its animation and link. |
| None | Through Slides' own **Transparent**. | The object, with its animation and link. |
| Gradient, or a stroke with opacity | Through Slides' paint format, from a temporary copy that is removed again. | The object, with its animation and link. |
| Gradient on an object whose text has more than one style | The object is replaced. | The text styles. Animations and links on the object are not kept, and the extension says so. |

Each of these is one undo step. See [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md).

## Stroke weight

| Control | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Weight field |  | Type a weight in pixels and press Enter. 0 removes the stroke. The slide shows the weight as you type. A weight that is not one of Slides' own (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24) replaces the object. |
| Thinner stroke | Option+Shift+[ | Steps down through Slides' weights: 24, 16, 12, 8, 4, 3, 2, 1 pixels. |
| Thicker stroke | Option+Shift+] | Steps up through the same weights. |
| **Stroke on / off** | Option+Shift+/ | Removes the stroke or puts it back. |
| **Stroke position** |  | Inside, centre or outside. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#position). |

## Changing a number by dragging

Hold Option and drag left or right across a number field to change the value. Add Shift for steps of ten. This works on the weight field and on every field in the Edit Shape pill.

## Rotate and resize

The toolbar has no rotate or resize buttons. Outside Edit Shape, use Slides' own shortcuts. Inside Edit Shape, use [the box](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#smart-box).

| Command | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Rotate 15° left or right | Option+Left Arrow, Option+Right Arrow |
| Rotate 1° left or right | Option+Shift+Left Arrow, Option+Shift+Right Arrow |
| Make larger | Command+Control+K |
| Make smaller | Command+Control+J |

## See also

- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#exact-values)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md#paint)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# The command palette

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Press Command+\ to open a searchable list of every command with its shortcut. Type a few letters, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to run the command.

**To run a command by name**

1. Press Command+\, or click **Commands** on the toolbar.
2. Type part of the command's name. The list narrows as you type.
3. Press Up Arrow or Down Arrow to move, and Enter to run the command.

Press Esc, or Command+\ again, to close the palette without running anything.

![The command palette open over a slide: a search field reading Type a command and a list grouped under Shape tools, Outline, Arrange, and Align and distribute, each command with its shortcut at the right](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/command-palette.jpg)
Figure 1. The command palette. Shortcuts are listed at the right of each command.

## What the palette lists

Commands are grouped: Shape tools, Outline, Arrange, Align and distribute, Combine, Group, Fill and stroke, Transform and stroke. The full list with descriptions is in [Command reference](https://svgslid.es/docs/commands.md).

Commands that need a selection are dimmed while nothing is selected. The Pen, the Layers panel, the toolbar and the theme builder can be opened at any time.

## See also

- [Command reference](https://svgslid.es/docs/commands.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.
