# Undo and redo

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

One press of Command+Z undoes a whole change made by the extension, even when the change took several steps inside Slides. Shift+Command+Z or Command+Y redoes it in one press.

## Changes that undo in one press

- Union, Subtract, Intersect and Exclude.
- Mask image with shape.
- Outline stroke, Outline text and Restore outlined text.
- Stroke position, a typed stroke weight, Thinner stroke and Thicker stroke.
- A colour, opacity or gradient set in the colour panel, and text colour.
- Replace a colour, on one slide or across all slides.
- Moving the picture under its mask.
- Restacking in the Layers panel.
- Aligning one object to a slide edge.
- A whole Edit Shape or pen session, from opening the editor to **Done**.

Align and distribute with several objects are a single Slides step to begin with.

## How to undo and redo

| To do this | Press |
|---|---|
| Undo the extension's last change | Command+Z |
| Redo it | Shift+Command+Z or Command+Y |

Slides' own **Undo** and **Redo** buttons do the same. You can undo and redo back and forth through a chain of the extension's changes, one press each.

## When Slides' own undo takes over

The one-press undo applies while the slide is as the extension left it. If you change the slide yourself after one of the extension's changes, Slides' own undo takes over from there, and a change that took several steps then takes several presses to undo. See [PRB: COMMAND+Z undoes only part of a combine or outline](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/undo-takes-several-presses.md).

While you are typing in a text box, Command+Z is always Slides' own.

## Inside Edit Shape

Inside the editor, Command+Z undoes one edit at a time: one moved point, one pen point. After **Done**, the whole session is one step on the slide.

## See also

- [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#done)
- [PRB: COMMAND+Z undoes only part of a combine or outline](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/undo-takes-several-presses.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Editing Slides' own shapes

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later.

Edit Shape also opens on objects you did not bring in as SVG: shapes from Slides' shape menu, arrows, callouts, lines, text boxes and WordArt. It converts the object into custom shapes first, and tells you what that costs before you start.

## How it works

Double-click the object. Slides does what it always does: it starts text editing or steps into the group. The **Edit Shape** button also appears, with a note of the cost in grey beside it, for example "text becomes outlines". Click the button to convert the object and open the editor.

The result looks the same as the original. It is a drawing made of custom shapes and is no longer the original preset, line or WordArt.

## What each object becomes

| Object | After conversion | What is lost |
|---|---|---|
| A shape-menu shape with one outline: arrow, callout, star, rounded rectangle | One shape | Adjustment handles, the small yellow diamonds. |
| A shaded shape: cube, can | A group. A cube becomes 4 shapes, a can 3. | Automatic shading. The shades are kept as flat colours. |
| A line or connector with ends | A group: the stroke and each arrowhead | Connection points. Arrowheads become separate shapes. |
| A shape with text in it | One shape, text kept |  |
| A text box | One shape with no fill and no stroke, text kept |  |
| WordArt | A group of letter outlines | The text. The letters can be reshaped but not retyped. |

Text inside a shape stays editable after conversion.

## Cancel and Done

**Cancel** puts the original object back. **Done** keeps the converted shapes.

> **Caution:** After **Done** the conversion is one-way. To get the original back, undo.

## Not handled

- Gradient and pattern fills, fill transparency, dash styles and shadows are not carried over.
- Images, video and charts cannot be converted.

## See also

- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Rounding corners](https://svgslid.es/docs/round-corners.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md)
- [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes (SVG to Slides Documentation, User's Guide). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Web Uploader

Applies to: SVG to Slides Web Uploader.

The Web Uploader converts SVG files on a web page, with nothing to install. Upload one file or a batch and get a Google Drive link to a file with one slide per SVG, every path a native shape.

**To convert SVG files online**

1. Open [svgslid.es/convert](https://svgslid.es/convert).
2. Drop your .svg files on the upload area, or click it to browse. Each file becomes one slide.
3. Optional: type a Google account address. The file is then shared straight to that account.
4. Click **Convert**. A link to the file in Google Drive appears.

![The Web Uploader page with a dashed upload area reading Drop SVG files here or click to browse, an optional Google account field and a Convert button](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/web-uploader.jpg)
Figure 1. The Web Uploader.

## Keeping the file

Links stay active for 7 days. After that the file is deleted.

**To keep a converted file**

1. Open the link.
2. In Google Drive, choose **File › Make a copy**.

The copy belongs to your account and does not expire.

## How it differs from the extension

|  | Web Uploader | Chrome extension |
|---|---|---|
| Where the result goes | A new file, one slide per SVG | The slide you have open |
| Gradients | Kept as gradients | Kept as gradients since version 1.4.0. First colour only before that |
| SVG text | Outlined into shapes. Not editable as text. | Not converted |
| Line icons that set the stroke on the whole SVG | Converted. Strokes become filled outline shapes. | Not converted |
| Where conversion runs | On the svgslid.es server | In your browser |
| Batch size | A batch | Up to 25 files per drop |

Clip paths, masks, patterns, filters and transparency do not come through on either. See [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md).

## What happens to your files

Uploaded SVG files are held only while the request runs and are deleted when it finishes. The converted file is stored in Google Drive for 7 days and shared by link. See [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#web-uploader).

## See also

- [Workspace Add-on](https://svgslid.es/docs/add-on.md)
- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md)
- [PRB: A Web Uploader link stops working after 7 days](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/web-uploader-link-expired.md)
- [Guide: SVG to Google Slides converter](https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-to-google-slides-converter)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader (SVG to Slides Documentation, Web Uploader and Add-on). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Workspace Add-on

Applies to: SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

The add-on inserts SVG files from a dialog inside Google Slides. Pick your files, copy, and paste. Every path lands as a native shape on the slide you have open.

**To insert SVG files with the add-on**

1. In Google Slides, choose **Insert SVGs** from the **Extensions** menu, or click the add-on's icon in the side panel.
2. Pick your .svg files. They convert as you select them.
3. Click **Copy**, or press Enter.
4. Press Command+V. The shapes land on the slide you have open.

![The add-on dialog titled Insert SVGs with four shape thumbnails, the line Ready, click below or press Enter to copy, and a Copy button](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/add-on-dialog.jpg)
Figure 1. The add-on dialog. *Illustration.*

## Good to know

- Select more than one file and they land side by side on the current slide.
- A gradient comes through as its first colour. For full gradients use the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md).
- The add-on is installed from the Google Workspace Marketplace: [svgslid.es/addon](https://svgslid.es/addon).

## What the add-on can access

| Access | Used for |
|---|---|
| The current presentation's page size | Sizing the inserted shapes to fit the slide. |
| Showing a dialog | The **Insert SVGs** dialog. |
| Calling the svgslid.es converter | Converting the files you select. |

The add-on has no access to Google Drive and does not read or change the content of your presentation through Google's API. The shapes are written to your clipboard and you paste them. See [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#add-on).

## See also

- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md)
- [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/add-on (SVG to Slides Documentation, Web Uploader and Add-on). Last reviewed November 20, 2026.

# Keyboard shortcuts

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later. Editor keys also apply to version 1.2.0 unless they name a 1.3.0 tool..

All shortcuts, with the Mac and Windows keys side by side. The extension's own shortcuts work while objects are selected and you are not typing in a text box. Five of them work at any time.

> **Note:** The extension's shortcuts are off while the cursor is in a text box, so that typing Option+Shift characters still works. Click the slide or an object first.

## Tools and panels

These work whether or not anything is selected.

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Show or hide the toolbar | Option+\ | Alt+\ |
| Command palette | Command+\ | Ctrl+\ |
| Show or hide Layers | Option+1 | Alt+1 |
| Pen | Option+Shift+P | Alt+Shift+P |
| Theme builder, and back | Option+Shift+M | Alt+Shift+M |
| Edit Shape | Double-click, then Edit Shape | Double-click, then Edit Shape |
| Select inside a group | Command-click | Ctrl-click |
| Undo one of the extension's changes | Command+Z | Ctrl+Z |
| Redo it | Shift+Command+Z | Ctrl+Shift+Z |

## Align and distribute

With objects selected. Not while typing in a text box.

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Align left | Option+A | Alt+A |
| Align centres horizontally | Option+H | Alt+H |
| Align right | Option+D | Alt+D |
| Align top | Option+W | Alt+W |
| Align middles vertically | Option+V | Alt+V |
| Align bottom | Option+S | Alt+S |
| Distribute horizontal spacing | Option+Shift+H | Alt+Shift+H |
| Distribute vertical spacing | Option+Shift+V | Alt+Shift+V |

## Combine

With two or more shapes selected.

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Union | Option+Shift+U | Alt+Shift+U |
| Subtract | Option+Shift+S | Alt+Shift+S |
| Intersect | Option+Shift+I | Alt+Shift+I |
| Exclude | Option+Shift+E | Alt+Shift+E |

## Group and mask

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Group | Command+Option+G | Ctrl+Alt+G |
| Ungroup | Shift+Command+Option+G | Ctrl+Alt+Shift+G |
| Mask image with shape | Option+Shift+K | Alt+Shift+K |

## Outline

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Outline stroke | Option+Command+O | Ctrl+Alt+O |
| Outline text | Option+Command+T | Ctrl+Alt+T |
| Restore outlined text | Option+Command+T | Ctrl+Alt+T |

## Fill and stroke

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Fill colour | Option+Shift+F | Alt+Shift+F |
| Stroke colour | Option+Shift+L | Alt+Shift+L |
| Stroke on / off | Option+Shift+/ | Alt+Shift+/ |
| Thinner stroke | Option+Shift+[ | Alt+Shift+[ |
| Thicker stroke | Option+Shift+] | Alt+Shift+] |

## Arrange, rotate and resize

These are Google Slides' own shortcuts. The toolbar and the command palette list them, and Slides carries them out.

| Command | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Bring to front | Shift+Command+Up Arrow | Ctrl+Shift+Up Arrow |
| Bring forward | Command+Up Arrow | Ctrl+Up Arrow |
| Send backward | Command+Down Arrow | Ctrl+Down Arrow |
| Send to back | Shift+Command+Down Arrow | Ctrl+Shift+Down Arrow |
| Rotate 15° left or right | Option+Left Arrow | Alt+Left Arrow |
| Rotate 1° left or right | Option+Shift+Left Arrow | Alt+Shift+Left Arrow |
| Make larger | Command+Control+K | Ctrl+Alt+K |
| Make smaller | Command+Control+J | Ctrl+Alt+J |

## In Edit Shape and the pen

On Windows use Ctrl for Command, Alt for Option and Backspace for Delete.

| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Select tool | V |
| Pen tool | P |
| Move a point or handle in 45° steps | Hold Shift while dragging |
| Move one curve handle on its own | Hold Option while dragging it |
| Switch a point between smooth and corner | Double-click the point |
| Select all points | Command+A |
| Delete selected points. In the pen, remove the last point. | Delete |
| Nudge | Arrow keys. Shift for ten times the step. |
| Undo, redo | Command+Z, Shift+Command+Z |
| Zoom in, zoom out, 100% | Command+Plus, Command+Minus, Command+0. Or pinch. |
| Pan | Hold Spacebar and drag, or scroll |
| Show or hide the grid | Command+' |
| Ignore snapping for one move | Hold Command |
| Change a number by dragging | Hold Option and drag across the field. Shift for steps of ten. |
| Round corners in 10 pixel steps | Hold Shift while dragging a corner circle |
| Scale in proportion, or from the centre | Shift, Option while dragging the box |
| Skew | Command and drag an edge of the box |
| Rotate | Command and drag a corner of the box |
| Pen: close the shape | Click the first point |
| Pen: leave the path open | Enter or Esc |
| Done | Enter, or Esc with nothing selected |

## Where the keys come from

Align and distribute use the keys Figma uses. Rotate, resize, arrange, group and ungroup are Google Slides' own shortcuts. The rest are the extension's.

## See also

- [Command reference](https://svgslid.es/docs/commands.md)

- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)

# Command reference

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Every command the toolbar and the command palette offer, by group, with what each one needs selected.

## Tools and panels

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Show or hide the toolbar | Opens or closes the toolbar. | Nothing | Option+\ |
| Command palette | Lists every command with its shortcut. | Nothing | Command+\ |
| Show or hide Layers | Opens or closes the Layers panel. | Nothing | Option+1 |
| Pen | Draws new shapes, or opens the editor on the selection with the pen active. | Nothing | Option+Shift+P |
| Theme builder, and back | Opens Slides' theme builder on the slide's layout, or returns to the slide. | Nothing | Option+Shift+M |
| Edit Shape | Opens the point editor on the selection. Double-click a shape, then click Edit Shape. | A shape |  |
| Select inside a group | Command-click selects the innermost object under the pointer. Shift+Command-click adds. | Nothing |  |
| Undo one of the extension's changes | Undoes a multi-step change in one press. | Right after the change | Command+Z |
| Redo it | Redoes it in one press. Command+Y does the same. | Right after an undo | Shift+Command+Z |

## Align and distribute

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Align left | Aligns left edges. One object: to the slide's left edge. | One object or more | Option+A |
| Align centres horizontally | Aligns centres on a vertical line. One object: centres it on the page. | One object or more | Option+H |
| Align right | Aligns right edges. One object: to the slide's right edge. | One object or more | Option+D |
| Align top | Aligns top edges. One object: to the slide's top edge. | One object or more | Option+W |
| Align middles vertically | Aligns middles on a horizontal line. One object: centres it on the page. | One object or more | Option+V |
| Align bottom | Aligns bottom edges. One object: to the slide's bottom edge. | One object or more | Option+S |
| Distribute horizontal spacing | Evens out the horizontal gaps. | Three objects or more | Option+Shift+H |
| Distribute vertical spacing | Evens out the vertical gaps. | Three objects or more | Option+Shift+V |

## Combine

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Union | One shape covering everything the selected shapes cover. | Two shapes or more | Option+Shift+U |
| Subtract | The bottom shape with the shapes above it cut out. | Two shapes or more | Option+Shift+S |
| Intersect | Only the area where the shapes overlap. | Two shapes or more | Option+Shift+I |
| Exclude | Everything except the area where the shapes overlap. | Two shapes or more | Option+Shift+E |

## Group and mask

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group | Groups the selection. | Two objects or more | Command+Option+G |
| Ungroup | Ungroups the selected group. | A group | Shift+Command+Option+G |
| Mask image with shape | The shape on top cuts out the picture under it. On a masked picture or its group, opens the picture for moving and resizing under the mask. | One image and one shape or group, or a masked picture | Option+Shift+K |

## Outline

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline stroke | Turns a stroke into a filled shape. | A shape or line with a stroke | Option+Command+O |
| Outline text | Turns text into shapes. | An object with text | Option+Command+T |
| Restore outlined text | Puts outlined text back as live text. | Text outlined on this computer | Option+Command+T |

## Fill and stroke

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fill colour | Opens the colour panel on the fill. With text highlighted, sets the text colour. With nothing selected, opens Replace a colour. | A shape, highlighted text, or nothing | Option+Shift+F |
| Stroke colour | Opens the colour panel on the stroke. | A shape or line | Option+Shift+L |
| Stroke on / off | Removes the stroke or puts it back. | A shape or line | Option+Shift+/ |
| Thinner stroke | Steps the stroke weight down. | A shape or line | Option+Shift+[ |
| Thicker stroke | Steps the stroke weight up. | A shape or line | Option+Shift+] |
| Centre stroke | Puts the stroke back on the outline. | A closed shape with a stroke |  |
| Inside stroke | Moves the stroke inside the outline. | A closed shape with a stroke |  |
| Outside stroke | Moves the stroke outside the outline. | A closed shape with a stroke |  |

## Arrange, rotate and resize

| Command | What it does | Needs selected | Shortcut (Mac) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bring to front | Moves the selection to the top of the stack. | An object | Shift+Command+Up Arrow |
| Bring forward | Moves the selection up one place. | An object | Command+Up Arrow |
| Send backward | Moves the selection down one place. | An object | Command+Down Arrow |
| Send to back | Moves the selection to the bottom of the stack. | An object | Shift+Command+Down Arrow |
| Rotate 15° left or right | Rotates the selection. Option+Right Arrow rotates the other way. | An object | Option+Left Arrow |
| Rotate 1° left or right | Rotates in fine steps. Option+Shift+Right Arrow rotates the other way. | An object | Option+Shift+Left Arrow |
| Make larger | Resizes the selection up. | An object | Command+Control+K |
| Make smaller | Resizes the selection down. | An object | Command+Control+J |


## Messages

When a command cannot run, the extension shows a short message under the toolbar that says what to select. Examples: "Select two or more objects to group", "Select three or more objects to distribute", "Nothing selected has text".

## See also

- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://svgslid.es/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)

- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md)

# SVG feature support

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides; SVG to Slides Web Uploader.

Paths, basic shapes, arcs, nested transforms and even-odd cut-outs convert in every product. Gradients convert in the Web Uploader and, since version 1.4.0, in the extension, which also keeps transparency. Text converts only in the Web Uploader. Masks, patterns and filters do not convert.

Tested November 11, 2026 on 20 sample files. Per-file table and sample files: https://svgslid.es/specs.md

## Converts

| SVG feature | Chrome extension and add-on | Web Uploader |
|---|---|---|
| One filled path | Converts. | Works |
| Circle, rounded rectangle and path in three colours | Converts. | Works |
| rect, circle, ellipse, polygon, polyline, line | Lines and polylines become filled outline shapes | Works. Lines and polylines become filled outline shapes |
| Line icon with the stroke set on the root <svg> (Lucide and Feather style) | Strokes become filled outline shapes | Works. Strokes become filled outline shapes |
| Arc commands (A and a) | Converts. | Works |
| translate, rotate and scale on nested groups | Converts. | Works |
| fill-rule="evenodd" cut-outs | Converts. | Works |
| Linear gradient fill | Kept as a gradient | Works. Kept as a gradient |
| Radial gradient fill | Kept as a gradient | Works. Kept as a gradient |
| Colours set by CSS classes in a <style> block (Illustrator style) | Converts. | Partly. Shapes kept, colours become black |
| Figma-style frame clip and white background | Frame clip and background skipped | Works. Frame clip and background skipped |
| clip-path that crops a shape | Cropped to the clip shape | Partly. Clip ignored; the full shape shows |
| <use> referencing a <symbol> (icon sprites) | Converts. | Not converted. Not converted |
| fill-opacity | Transparency kept | Partly. Shapes kept, transparency lost |
| stroke="currentColor" | Strokes become filled outline shapes | Partly. Converted, but black instead of the inherited colour |
| rgb(), named, short hex and hsl() colours | Converts. | Partly. hsl() becomes black; the rest are exact |

## Converts in part

| SVG feature | Chrome extension and add-on | Web Uploader |
|---|---|---|
| mask that cuts a hole | Mask ignored | Partly. Mask ignored |
| Pattern fill | Shape kept, filled black | Partly. Shape kept, filled black |
| Drop-shadow filter | Shape kept, shadow dropped | Partly. Shape kept, shadow dropped |

## Does not convert

| SVG feature | Chrome extension and add-on | Web Uploader |
|---|---|---|
| <text> element | Not converted | Works. Outlined into shapes, not editable text |


## Reading the table

The extension column is for version 1.4.0. Version 1.3.1 added outline icon sets, colours from CSS classes, clip paths and use with symbol. Version 1.4.0 added gradients and transparency. The Workspace Add-on runs the earlier converter: it fills a gradient with its first colour and does not keep transparency. See [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md#javascript).

## Getting a file to convert

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| A gradient arrives as one colour | Update the extension to version 1.4.0, which keeps gradients, or use the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). See [FIX: A gradient arrives as one solid colour](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/gradient-becomes-solid-colour.md). |
| Text is missing | Convert the text to outlines in your design tool before exporting, or use the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). |
| A line icon inserts nothing | Update the extension to version 1.3.1 or later. See [PRB: A line icon inserts nothing](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/line-icon-inserts-nothing.md). |
| Colours arrive black | Export with colours written on each element. See [PRB: Shapes arrive black](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/colours-arrive-black.md). |
| A masked shape shows in full | Apply the mask in your design tool before exporting, or mask it on the slide with [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md) and [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md). |

Have a file that does not convert? Send it to the address on the [Support](https://svgslid.es/support) page.

## See also

- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md)
- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md)
- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md)
- [Specs: tested compatibility table](https://svgslid.es/specs#compatibility)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility (SVG to Slides Documentation, Reference). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Permissions and data handling

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

The extension has no access to your Google account and runs only on Google Slides editor pages. Version 1.3.0 holds one Chrome permission, storage, and converts every file inside your browser.

## Chrome permissions by version

| Version | Chrome permissions | Where SVG files are converted |
|---|---|---|
| 1.3.0 | storage | In your browser, always. |
| 1.2.0 | storage, and one host permission for the svgslid.es converter | In your browser. The converter on the server was a fallback if in-browser conversion was unavailable. |
| 1.0.1 | One host permission for the svgslid.es converter | As 1.2.0. |

No version requests a Google sign-in or any Google account permission. The extension cannot read your Drive or reach your presentations through Google's API.

## What the extension reads

- The .svg files you drop on the slide.
- When you use Edit Shape or a shape command, the objects you selected on the open slide: their outlines, fill and stroke. This is read in your browser.

## What is stored on your computer

The storage permission keeps these items in Chrome on the computer you use. None of them is part of the presentation.

| Item | Used by |
|---|---|
| Whether the toolbar is open or closed, and whether Layers is open | [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md) |
| Snapping settings | [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md) |
| Layer names | [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md#stored) |
| Recent colours | [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md#panel) |
| The original text of outlined text | [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#restore) |
| The original outline of shapes whose stroke was moved inside or outside | [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#position) |
| Whether the update note has been shown | [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#updates) |

## Network requests in version 1.3.0

SVG files are not uploaded. The extension makes one kind of network request: **Outline text** downloads the font it needs from Google Fonts. The request names the font family, weight and style and carries nothing from the presentation. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#fonts).

## Web Uploader

- The SVG files you upload are sent to the svgslid.es server, held while the request runs, and deleted when it finishes.
- The converted file is stored in Google Drive for 7 days and shared with anyone who has the link.
- If you type a Google account address, it is used once, to share the file to that account.

## Workspace Add-on

- The add-on reads the current presentation's page size, shows its dialog, and calls the svgslid.es converter. It has no Drive access.
- The files you select are sent to the server, held in memory while the request runs, and not kept.
- The result is written to your clipboard. You paste it.

> **Note:** The [Privacy Policy](https://svgslid.es/privacy) is the governing statement for all three products. This topic summarises it and adds the per-version detail.

## See also

- [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md)
- [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md)
- [Version history](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes.md)
- [Privacy Policy](https://svgslid.es/privacy)
- [Terms](https://svgslid.es/terms)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy (SVG to Slides Documentation, Reference). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Limits and known issues

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

The limits stated across this library, gathered in one place. Each one links to the topic that explains it.

## Inserting

| Limit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Files per drop | 25 in the extension. See [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#several). |
| Where shapes land | On the slide you have open. The extension and the add-on cannot create slides. |
| Gradients | Kept by the extension since version 1.4.0 and by the Web Uploader. First colour only in the add-on and in earlier versions of the extension. `gradientTransform` is not applied. |
| SVG text | Not converted by the extension or the add-on. Outlined by the Web Uploader. |
| Masks, patterns, filters | Not converted. See [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md). |

## Shape tools

| Limit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Combine and outline | Gradients, pattern fills, transparency and shadows are not carried into the result. Images, video and charts are refused. |
| Mask | Rotated images are not supported yet. Text must be outlined first. A fill on a whole mask group is refused. See [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md#limits). |
| Gradient on text with several styles | The object is replaced, so its animation and link are not kept. See [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md#applied). |
| Stroke weight | A weight that is not one of Slides' own replaces the object. See [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md#weight). |
| Gradient stops | One opacity for the whole fill. Slides does not keep an opacity per stop. |
| Replace a colour, all slides | Colours of slides far down a long filmstrip may not be listed until you scroll to them. See [Colour, gradients and stroke](https://svgslid.es/docs/fill-stroke.md#replace). |
| Pen | Point by point only. No freehand mode. |
| Skew | Available in Edit Shape only. |
| Layers | Only top-level rows can be dragged to restack. |
| Edit Shape | **Done** replaces the object, so animations and links on the original are not kept. See [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#done). |
| Converting Slides' own shapes | One-way. See [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md). |

## Kept on one computer

Layer names, snapping settings, recent colours, the memory that restores outlined text, and the memory of stroke position are kept on the computer you used. They do not travel with the presentation. Hiding an object in Layers affects only your view and ends when the page is reloaded. See [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#storage).

## Undo

One-press undo applies right after one of the extension's changes. If you change the slide in between, Slides' own undo takes over. See [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md#slides-undo).

## Web Uploader and add-on

| Limit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Web Uploader links | Deleted after 7 days. Make a copy to keep the file. |
| Add-on gradients | First colour only. |
| Add-on insert | Always ends with Command+V. A web page cannot paste for you. |

## See also

- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [All articles](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb.md)
- [Version 1.4.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-4-0.md#limits)
- [Version 1.3.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-3-0.md#limits)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/limits (SVG to Slides Documentation, Reference). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Glossary

Applies to: All SVG to Slides documentation.

Terms used in this library, in alphabetical order.

### Add-on {#add-on} The SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on. It runs inside Google Slides from the Extensions menu. See [Workspace Add-on](https://svgslid.es/docs/add-on.md).

### Box {#box} The frame with handles around the selection in Edit Shape. Dragging it scales, stretches, skews or rotates. See [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md#smart-box).

### Combine {#combine} To make one shape from several with Union, Subtract, Intersect or Exclude. See [Combining shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/combine-shapes.md).

### Command palette {#command-palette} A searchable list of every command, opened with Command+\. See [The command palette](https://svgslid.es/docs/command-palette.md).

### Corner point {#corner-point} A point where the outline turns sharply. Drawn as a square in Edit Shape. Compare *smooth point*.

### Custom shape {#custom-shape} A Slides shape defined by its own outline, as opposed to a preset from the shape menu. Every shape SVG to Slides inserts is a custom shape or a polyline.

### Flatten {#flatten} What Slides does to an SVG placed on a slide without SVG to Slides: it turns the drawing into a picture made of pixels.

### Handle {#handle} One of the two control points beside a smooth point. Dragging a handle changes the curve on that side of the point.

### Layout {#layout} A slide design in the theme that slides are based on. Objects on a layout appear on every slide that uses it. See [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md).

### Mask {#mask} A shape used to cut a picture so that the picture shows only inside the shape. See [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md).

### Master {#master} The top level of a Slides theme. Objects on the master appear on every layout and slide. See [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md).

### Native shape {#native-shape} A shape that Slides treats as its own: it can be selected, filled, resized, grouped, used in themes and copied to Google Drawings.

### Outline {#outline} As a verb: to turn a stroke or text into filled shapes. As a noun: the path that defines a shape's edge. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md).

### Path {#path} In an SVG file, a sequence of lines and curves. Each path becomes one Slides shape.

### Pill {#pill} The small dark panel under the selection in Edit Shape that holds width, height, rotation and corner radius.

### Polyline {#polyline} A Slides shape made of straight segments, on which Slides' own Edit points command works. See [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md).

### Scrub {#scrub} To change a number by holding Option and dragging across its field.

### Smooth point {#smooth-point} A point where the outline curves through without a corner. Drawn as a circle in Edit Shape. It has two handles.

### Snapping {#snapping} Pulling a point onto a nearby point, pixel or grid line as you place or drag it. See [Snapping](https://svgslid.es/docs/snapping.md).

### Still copy {#still-copy} A picture of the slide that the extension shows while a change takes several steps, so that only the result is seen. See [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md).

### Stroke position {#stroke-position} Whether a stroke sits inside, on, or outside a shape's outline. See [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#position).

### Theme object {#theme-object} An object drawn on a slide that belongs to the slide's layout or master. It cannot be changed on the slide. See [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md).

### Toolbar {#toolbar} The strip of buttons the extension adds at the left edge of the slide canvas. See [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md).

### Web Uploader {#web-uploader} The page at svgslid.es/convert that converts SVG files to a Drive file. See [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md).

## See also

- [Index](https://svgslid.es/docs/a-z-index.md)
- [Document conventions](https://svgslid.es/docs/conventions.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/glossary (SVG to Slides Documentation, Reference). Last reviewed November 20, 2026.

# How conversion works

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Conversion turns every drawable element of the SVG into a path, and every path into one Slides shape with one fill. The extension and the add-on write the shapes in Slides' own form. The Web Uploader writes a presentation file.

## Stages

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1. Read | The SVG is parsed. Definitions, clip paths and masks are set aside, and so is a rectangle that only fills the canvas as a background. |
| 2. Paint | Fill and stroke are worked out for each element, including values inherited from the groups around it. |
| 3. Shapes to paths | `rect`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline` and `polygon` become path data. |
| 4. Arcs to curves | Arc commands are converted into cubic Bézier curves. |
| 5. Strokes to outlines | A stroke with a width is expanded into a filled outline, because the shape that lands has one fill. |
| 6. Transforms | `translate`, `rotate` and `scale` on the element and on its groups are applied to the points. |
| 7. Write | Each path becomes one shape with a tight bounding box. Shapes from one file are grouped. |

## Two outputs

|  | Extension and add-on | Web Uploader |
|---|---|---|
| Output | Slides' own shape data, handed to the open slide. See [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md). | A presentation file with one slide per SVG, each path a custom-geometry shape. |
| Gradients | Extension 1.4.0: written as Slides gradients, with the stops re-timed onto the line Slides draws. Add-on and earlier extension versions: the first colour stop becomes a solid fill. | Kept as gradients. |
| Text and some strokes | Not converted. | Outlined on the server before conversion. |

## The JavaScript converter in version 1.3.0

Up to version 1.2.0 the extension carried a Python runtime compiled to WebAssembly and ran the same Python converter the server runs. That runtime was most of the installed size.

Version 1.3.0 replaces it with a JavaScript converter that follows the Python one line for line, including its rounding rules and its error cases. The two were compared before release:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All 138 SVG files in the project's repository, and multi-file drops | Output identical, byte for byte. |
| 3,000 randomly generated SVG files | Identical except for 3 files with a perfect half-ellipse arc, where the last bit of a floating-point result decides whether the same shape is written as two curve pieces or three. |

The installed size fell from 14 MB to 1.1 MB. With no runtime to fall back from, the server fallback and its host permission were removed. See [Version 1.3.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-3-0.md#packaging).

## Why some features do not convert

A Slides shape has one outline and one fill. SVG features that depend on something else, such as a clip path, a mask, a filter, a pattern or per-element transparency, have no place to go and are dropped or ignored. Colours written as `hsl()` are not parsed and arrive black. The tested results are in [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md).

## See also

- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md)
- [Point precision](https://svgslid.es/docs/point-precision.md)
- [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works (SVG to Slides Documentation, Technical Notes). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# How shapes reach the slide

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

The extension never calls a Google API. It hands shapes to Slides in the form Slides itself uses when you copy and paste a shape, so Slides treats them as its own. That is why the extension needs no Google permission.

## The route

When you copy a shape in Google Slides, Slides writes it to the clipboard in a form of its own. Paste that data back and Slides rebuilds the shape. SVG to Slides writes the same form from an SVG's paths and gives it to Slides. Slides accepts it as if it had copied the shapes itself.

No request goes to the Slides API or to Drive, and no OAuth scope is involved.

## How the hand-over is made

| Product and version | Hand-over |
|---|---|
| Extension 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 | The extension placed the data on your clipboard at your click. You pressed Command+V. |
| Extension 1.2.0 and later | The extension delivers the data to the Slides tab the way a paste does. If Slides does not accept it, the extension falls back to your clipboard and asks for Command+V. |
| Add-on | You click **Copy**, then press Command+V. A dialog in a web page cannot paste for you. |

## Reading the selection

Edit Shape and the shape commands need to know what is selected. They read it the way a copy does: Slides hands over the same shape data, inside your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

## Replacing a shape

An edit, a combine or an outline ends by removing the original objects and handing Slides the result in the same place, then restoring its place in the stack. Slides records that as several steps. See [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md) for how those steps are hidden and undone as one.

## What follows from this route

- Shapes land on the slide you have open. The route cannot create slides.
- The result is a native object. A masked image, for example, is the same kind of object Slides makes when you crop an image to a shape: a shape filled with the picture.
- The form Slides uses is internal to Google and can change. The extension is built so that if a scripted hand-over stops working, it falls back to copy and Command+V.

## See also

- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md)
- [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md)
- [INFO: The extension asks you to press COMMAND+V](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/press-command-v-prompt.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide (SVG to Slides Documentation, Technical Notes). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Slides' Edit points and polylines

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Google Slides has an Edit points command of its own, which works on polylines. Inserted shapes with one outline and only straight segments land as polylines, so that command works on them. Curved shapes land as custom shapes. Use Edit Shape for those.

## The rule

A converted shape lands as a polyline when all three are true:

- It has a single outline, with no holes and no separate pieces.
- Every segment is a straight line.
- It has no more than 150 points.

Rectangles, polygons and other straight-edged closed paths meet the rule. Circles, curved icons and shapes with holes land as custom shapes.

## Why curved shapes are not polylines

Slides' point editor has no model for Bézier curves. These results come from inserting test shapes and dragging a point in each.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| A polyline that contains curves | It draws correctly when inserted. On the first point drag, Slides rewrites the whole outline as straight lines, and every curve control point becomes a corner. |
| A polyline with several outlines | Slides merges them into one outline, joining the outer and inner parts with stray diagonal edges. |
| A shape of Slides' curve-tool kind, given curve data | Slides ignores the curve data and draws its own smooth line through every coordinate. A circle made of four curves comes out as a lumpy rounded square. |

So only shapes that Slides' editor can represent exactly are marked for it.

## A difference you can see

| Shape | Double-click in Slides |
|---|---|
| Custom shape | Gives a text cursor. The shape can hold text. |
| Polyline | Enters Slides' point editing. |

## Which editor to use

| To edit | Use |
|---|---|
| A straight-edged shape, corner by corner | Slides' own **Edit points**, or [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md). |
| Any shape with curves or holes | [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md). |
| A shape from Slides' shape menu | [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md), which converts it first. See [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md). |

## See also

- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)
- [Editing Slides' own shapes](https://svgslid.es/docs/convert-slides-shapes.md)
- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md)
- [INFO: Slides' own Edit points is offered for some inserted shapes only](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/edit-points-missing.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines (SVG to Slides Documentation, Technical Notes). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Point precision: small SVGs keep their detail

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

From version 1.3.0 every inserted shape carries its points at full precision, whatever size it lands at. An icon dropped at 12 pixels can be enlarged later and keeps every curve.

## The problem before 1.3.0

Slides stores an inserted shape's points as they arrive and resizes the shape by changing its transform. It does not recalculate the points. Earlier versions wrote the points at the size of the drop, so those points were all the detail the shape ever had. An icon that landed 12 pixels wide carried 12 pixels' worth of positions, and enlarging it showed the rounding.

## What 1.3.0 does

Each shape's points are written in a frame of its own, about 100,000 units across, and the shape's transform scales that frame down to the size on the slide. The points are the same whatever the size.

Slides keeps a transform's scale to four decimal places. A scale of 0.047625 comes back as 0.0476. The converter therefore rounds the scale to four places first and sizes the frame to fit that scale exactly, so nothing shifts when Slides stores the shape.

![A slide zoomed to 400 percent showing a large palm icon with smooth, clean curves](https://svgslid.es/static/docs/img/small-svg-detail.jpg)
Figure 1. A small icon after enlarging, viewed at 400% zoom. *Illustration.*

## Checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The 138 SVG files in the project's repository | Every shape lands within 0.01 pixel of where it landed before the change. |
| A 12 pixel, two-shape icon enlarged about 700 times with Slides' own resize | The shape kept its full-precision points. |

> **Note:** The add-on still writes points at the size of the insert.

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#size)
- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md)
- [Version 1.3.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-3-0.md#converter)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/point-precision (SVG to Slides Documentation, Technical Notes). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# How multi-step changes run and undo

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

A combine, an outline, a mask or an Edit Shape session reaches Slides as several steps: remove, insert, restack. The extension shows a still copy of the slide while they run, so you see only the result, and it counts the steps so that one Command+Z undoes them all.

## The still copy

While a change runs, the extension lays a still picture of the slide over the canvas, under its own toolbar. Slides' toolbar is held still too. The copy includes the selection box, so the selection does not blink. When the last step has finished, the copy is removed and the finished slide shows.

Objects hidden in the Layers panel stay hidden in the copy.

For Align and Distribute the copy is drawn with the objects already at their destination. The slide changes once, straight to the result.

## Slides' own commands for moving

Align, Distribute and Center on page are run from Slides' own Arrange menu, which the extension keeps invisible while it uses it. Each is one Slides step. Nothing is deleted or reinserted.

This matters for images. An image that is deleted and reinserted from copied data can lose its picture, so anything that moves an image goes through Slides' own commands.

## One object to a slide edge

Slides' Align needs something to align to. To align a single object to an edge of the slide, the extension inserts a 1 pixel square with no fill and no line at the corner it needs, selects it with the object, runs Slides' Align, takes the object out of the selection and deletes the square. The steps run behind the still copy and undo as one. No extra object is left in the presentation.

## One-press undo

The extension notes the slide before and after each of its changes and counts the Slides steps the change made. If you press Command+Z right after, it walks Slides' own undo back that many steps, behind the still copy. Redo walks forward the same way.

Two rules keep this safe:

- It never presses undo more times than the change made steps.
- It applies only while the slide is as the extension left it. If you have changed the slide since, Slides' own undo is used, one step per press.

## See also

- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [Aligning and distributing](https://svgslid.es/docs/align-distribute.md)
- [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md)
- [PRB: COMMAND+Z undoes only part of a combine or outline](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/undo-takes-several-presses.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy (SVG to Slides Documentation, Technical Notes). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: An SVG placed in Google Slides becomes a flat image

Article ID: Q100101. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: Google Slides; SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Google Slides has no SVG import, so an SVG placed on a slide is flattened into a picture. To keep it as vectors, insert it with SVG to Slides: drag the file onto the slide with the Chrome extension, or convert it with the Web Uploader.

## Symptoms

An SVG placed on a slide without SVG to Slides behaves as one picture:

- It blurs or shows pixels when enlarged.
- Its parts cannot be selected or recoloured.
- Slides offers it picture options only.

## Cause

Google Slides does not keep SVG files as vectors. It flattens the drawing into a picture on the way in.

## Resolution

Insert the file as native shapes with one of the three products.

| Product | Do this |
|---|---|
| Chrome extension | Drag the .svg file onto the slide and click where it goes. See [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md). |
| Web Uploader | Upload the file and open the Drive link. See [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). |
| Workspace Add-on | Choose **Insert SVGs** from the Extensions menu. See [Workspace Add-on](https://svgslid.es/docs/add-on.md). |

## Status

This is how Google Slides behaves.

## More information

There are two manual routes that need no extension: convert the SVG to EMF, open it in Google Drawings and copy the shapes across; or insert it in PowerPoint, convert it to a shape, save, and open the file in Slides. The guide [How to insert an SVG into Google Slides](https://svgslid.es/guides/insert-svg-into-google-slides) walks through both.

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md)
- [What SVG to Slides does](https://svgslid.es/docs/overview.md)
- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [Guide: Does Google Slides support SVG?](https://svgslid.es/guides/does-google-slides-support-svg)
- [Guide: SVG vs PNG in Google Slides](https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-vs-png-google-slides)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/svg-becomes-a-flat-image (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# FIX: A gradient arrives as one solid colour

Article ID: Q100102. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.3.1; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Versions of the Chrome extension before 1.4.0, and the add-on, fill each shape with the gradient's first colour. Version 1.4.0 of the extension keeps linear and radial gradients. The Web Uploader has always kept them.

## Symptoms

A shape that has a linear or radial gradient in the SVG lands with one flat colour. A radial gradient with a white centre lands white.

## Cause

Extension versions before 1.4.0 and the add-on write each shape with a single fill. They use the first colour stop of the gradient.

## Resolution

**To keep the gradient**

1. Update the extension to version 1.4.0 or later. Chrome does this on its own. To check, see [HOWTO: Find which version of the extension is installed](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/which-version.md).
2. Insert the file again. Linear and radial gradients arrive as Slides gradients, and transparency is kept.

If you use the add-on, or cannot update, convert the file with the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md), make a copy of the Drive file, and copy the shapes into your presentation.

## Status

Fixed in version 1.4.0 of the Chrome extension. The add-on still fills with the first colour. A `gradientTransform` on the gradient is not applied.

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#converts)
- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md#partly)
- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md#outputs)
- [Version 1.4.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-4-0.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/gradient-becomes-solid-colour (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: Text in an SVG does not appear on the slide

Article ID: Q100103. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

The extension and the add-on do not convert SVG text elements. Convert the text to outlines in your design tool before exporting, or use the Web Uploader, which outlines text into shapes.

## Symptoms

The shapes of the SVG land on the slide. Words that were text in the SVG are not there.

## Cause

The extension and the add-on convert paths and basic shapes. They do not convert `<text>` elements.

## Resolution

Use either method.

- In your design tool, convert the text to outlines, then export the SVG again. The letters are then paths, and paths convert.
- Convert the file with the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). It outlines text on the server.

Either way the words arrive as shapes. They look the same but cannot be retyped. To have editable text, add a Slides text box.

## Status

This is a known limit of the extension and the add-on.

## See also

- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md#not-converted)
- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/text-missing-after-insert (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# PRB: A line icon inserts nothing

Article ID: Q100104. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides.

Icons that set their stroke once on the root svg element, or use stroke="currentColor", are not converted by the extension. Convert them with the Web Uploader, or outline the strokes in your design tool before exporting.

## Symptoms

You drop a line icon and click to place it. Nothing lands on the slide. Icon sets drawn with strokes, in the style of Lucide and Feather, are the usual case.

## Cause

These icons do not put a stroke on each path. They set it once on the root `<svg>` element, often as `stroke="currentColor"`. The extension's converter does not pick up a stroke set there, and it does not resolve `currentColor`, so it finds nothing to draw.

Strokes written on the elements themselves, with a stated colour, do convert. They land as filled outline shapes.

## Resolution

Use either method.

- Convert the icons with the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). It converts strokes set on the whole SVG into filled outline shapes. A `currentColor` stroke comes out black, and you can recolour it in Slides.
- In your design tool, outline the strokes, then export again.

## Status

This is a known limit of the extension and the add-on. Test files 04 and 17 on the [Specs page](https://svgslid.es/specs#compatibility) cover it.

## See also

- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md)
- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [How conversion works](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-conversion-works.md#stages)
- [Guide: SVG logos and icons in Slides themes](https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/line-icon-inserts-nothing (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# PRB: Shapes arrive black

Article ID: Q100105. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on for Google Slides; SVG to Slides Web Uploader.

Colours set by CSS classes in a style block, colours written as hsl(), and pattern fills are not read by the converter, so those shapes arrive black. Export with colours written on each element, or recolour the shapes in Slides.

## Symptoms

The shapes land with the right outlines but filled black.

## Cause

| In the SVG | Result |
|---|---|
| Colours set by CSS classes in a `<style>` block, as some Illustrator exports write them | Shapes kept, colours black. |
| Colours written as `hsl()` | Black. `rgb()`, named colours and short hex values are exact. |
| A pattern fill | Shape kept, filled black. |

## Resolution

- In your design tool's SVG export settings, choose the option that writes each colour on its own element instead of in a style sheet. It is often called presentation attributes.
- Or select the shapes in Slides and set their colours with the fill picker. Each path is its own shape.

## Status

This is a known limit in all three products.

## See also

- [SVG feature support](https://svgslid.es/docs/svg-compatibility.md#partly)
- [Quick start](https://svgslid.es/docs/quick-start.md#next)
- [Guide: Recolor SVGs in Google Slides](https://svgslid.es/guides/recolor-svg-in-google-slides)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/colours-arrive-black (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# INFO: The extension asks you to press COMMAND+V

Article ID: Q100106. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later.

The extension hands shapes to Google Slides the way a paste does. If Slides does not accept them, the extension places the shapes on your clipboard and asks you to press COMMAND+V to finish.

## Summary

Since version 1.2.0 a click inserts the shapes directly. The prompt is the fallback for when that does not go through.

## More information

| You see | Do this |
|---|---|
| A prompt to press Command+V after placing an SVG | Press Command+V. The shapes land. |
| "Press ⌘V to finish" after a shape command | Press Command+V. |
| "Couldn't replace the shapes. Delete them, then press ⌘V." | Delete the selected originals, then press Command+V. The result is on your clipboard. |
| "Slides didn't accept the result. Press ⌘Z to undo." | Press Command+Z and try the command again. |

On Windows the prompts name Ctrl in place of Command.

In versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 every insert ended with Command+V. That was the normal flow in those versions.

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#fallback)
- [How shapes reach the slide](https://svgslid.es/docs/how-shapes-reach-the-slide.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/press-command-v-prompt (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: Nothing is inserted when more than 25 files are dropped

Article ID: Q100107. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0.

The extension inserts up to 25 SVG files per drop. A larger drop inserts nothing and shows a message. Drop the files in batches of 25, or use the Web Uploader, which makes one slide per SVG.

## Symptoms

You drag more than 25 .svg files onto a slide. A message says there are too many files at once, and nothing lands.

## Cause

Files from one drop are laid out in a grid on the current slide. Past 25 files the grid stops being useful, so the extension refuses the drop.

## Resolution

- Drop the files in batches of 25 or fewer.
- Or convert the whole set with the [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md). It makes a file with one slide per SVG.

## Status

This behaviour is by design.

## See also

- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#several)
- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md#inserting)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/more-than-25-files (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# INFO: Slides' own Edit points is offered for some inserted shapes only

Article ID: Q100108. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.2.0 and later.

Slides' own Edit points works only on polylines. Inserted shapes with one outline and straight segments land as polylines. Curved shapes and shapes with holes do not, because Slides' point editor would damage them. Use Edit Shape for those.

## Summary

After inserting an SVG, some shapes offer Slides' **Edit points** and enter point editing on a double-click. Others give a text cursor on a double-click and have no **Edit points**.

## More information

Slides' point editor works with straight segments only. A shape is inserted as a polyline, which that editor accepts, only if it has a single outline, only straight segments, and no more than 150 points.

Every other shape is inserted as a custom shape. To edit its points, double-click it and click **Edit Shape**. See [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md).

The tests behind this rule are described in [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md).

## See also

- [Edit points and polylines](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-points-and-polylines.md)
- [Edit Shape: points and curves](https://svgslid.es/docs/edit-shape.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/edit-points-missing (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# PRB: COMMAND+Z undoes only part of a combine or outline

Article ID: Q100109. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

A combine, outline or mask is several steps inside Slides. The extension undoes them in one press only while the slide is as it left it. If you changed the slide afterwards, Slides' own undo takes over and goes one step per press. Keep pressing COMMAND+Z until the original returns.

## Symptoms

You press Command+Z after a Union, an Outline or a Mask. Shapes disappear or reappear one at a time and the slide passes through states you did not make.

## Cause

The change reached Slides as several steps: remove the originals, insert the result, restore its place in the stack. The extension undoes all of them in one press, but only right after the change. Once you change the slide yourself, the extension stops, because pressing undo for you could remove your own work.

## Resolution

Keep pressing Command+Z until the slide is back to where you want it. Nothing is lost. The steps are in Slides' own history.

## Status

This behaviour is by design.

## More information

In version 1.2.0, which had no one-press undo, undoing an Edit Shape session always took several presses.

## See also

- [Undo and redo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-redo.md)
- [Multi-step changes and undo](https://svgslid.es/docs/undo-and-still-copy.md#undo)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/undo-takes-several-presses (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.


---

# PRB: Layer names are missing on another computer

Article ID: Q100110. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Layer names are kept in Chrome on the computer where you set them. They are not saved in the presentation, so other people and other computers show the default names.

## Symptoms

You renamed objects in the Layers panel. On another computer, or for a colleague who opens the same presentation, the rows show their default names such as "Shape", "Image" or "Group of 3".

## Cause

The extension has no way to save a name inside the presentation without changing the objects. It keeps the names in Chrome's storage on the computer you used.

## Resolution

There is none. Rename the layers on the other computer if you need the names there.

## Status

This behaviour is by design.

## More information

The same applies to snapping settings, the memory that restores outlined text, and stroke position memory. Objects hidden with the eye are hidden only in your view. See [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#storage).

## See also

- [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md#stored)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#storage)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md#local)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/layer-names-missing (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# INFO: An object in Layers is greyed and marked M

Article ID: Q100111. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

The M marks a theme object: one that belongs to the slide's layout or master. It cannot be changed on the slide. Click its row twice to open Slides' theme builder on the layout or master that holds it.

## Summary

Some rows in the Layers panel are grey with an **M** badge, and clicking the object on the slide does nothing.

## More information

Slides draws layout and master objects on every slide that uses them. They can be edited only in the theme builder.

**To edit the object**

1. Click its row in the Layers panel.
2. Click the row again within 5 seconds. The theme builder opens with the object selected.
3. Press Option+Shift+M to return to the slide.

If the Layers panel says it could not select an object that is not marked **M**, click the object on the slide instead.

## See also

- [Theme objects](https://svgslid.es/docs/theme-objects.md)
- [The Layers panel](https://svgslid.es/docs/layers.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/object-greyed-with-m (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: Mask image with shape shows a message and does not mask

Article ID: Q100112. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Mask image with shape needs exactly one image and one shape or group selected, an image that is not rotated, and a mask that is a shape and not live text. The message under the toolbar says which condition failed.

## Symptoms

You press Option+Shift+K. The picture is not masked and a message appears under the toolbar.

## Cause and resolution

| Message | Cause | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| Select an image and a shape to mask it with | The selection has no image, or no shape. | Select the picture, then Shift-click the shape. |
| Select an image and the shape to mask it with (two objects) | More than two objects are selected. | Group the shapes first with Command+Option+G, then select the image and the group. |
| Straighten the image first: masking a rotated image isn't supported yet | The image is rotated. | Set the image's rotation back to 0, mask it, then rotate the result. |
| That shape is too thin to mask with | The shape has no width or no height, as a straight line has. | Use a shape that has both. |
| That shape has nothing to mask with | The object has no outline the extension can cut with. | Use a different shape. |
| Outline the text first (⌥⌘T), then mask with it | The mask is live text. | Press Option+Command+T to outline the text, then mask. |
| The mask has to be a shape (the other object is an image too) | Both selected objects are images. | Select one image and one shape. |
| Couldn't get the picture from Slides to mask it | Slides did not hand over the picture. | Try again. If it repeats, copy and paste the image, then mask the pasted copy. |

## Status

Masking rotated images is not supported in version 1.3.0.

## See also

- [Masking an image](https://svgslid.es/docs/mask-image.md)
- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#text)
- [Limits and known issues](https://svgslid.es/docs/limits.md#shape-tools)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/cannot-mask-image (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: Outline text reports that it could not get the font

Article ID: Q100113. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

Outline text reads letter shapes from the font. It downloads Google fonts from Google Fonts and asks Chrome for access to fonts installed on your computer. If neither works, allow font access when Chrome asks, or set the text in a Google font and outline it again.

## Symptoms

You press Option+Command+T. The text is not outlined, and a message says the extension could not get the font and suggests allowing font access or using a Google font.

## Cause

The font is not one that Google Fonts serves, and the extension could not read it from your computer. Either Chrome's font access prompt was declined, or the font is not installed.

## Resolution

Use either method.

- Press Option+Command+T again and choose **Allow** when Chrome asks for access to your fonts.
- Change the text to a Google font, then outline it.

## More information

For some system fonts that cannot be downloaded, the extension outlines the text with a font that has the same letter widths, and a note names the font it used. The outline then matches the text's spacing but not every letter shape.

## See also

- [Outlining strokes and text](https://svgslid.es/docs/outline-stroke-text.md#fonts)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#network)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/outline-text-font (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# PRB: A Web Uploader link stops working after 7 days

Article ID: Q100114. Last reviewed: November 20, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Web Uploader.

Files made by the Web Uploader are deleted after 7 days. To keep one, open the link within that time and choose File, Make a copy in Google Drive. If the link has expired, convert the SVG files again.

## Symptoms

A Drive link you received from the Web Uploader no longer opens.

## Cause

Converted files are stored for 7 days, then deleted by a daily clean-up.

## Resolution

**To keep a converted file**

1. Open the link within 7 days.
2. Choose **File › Make a copy**. The copy is yours and does not expire.

If the link has already expired, upload the SVG files again at [svgslid.es/convert](https://svgslid.es/convert).

## Status

This behaviour is by design.

## See also

- [Web Uploader](https://svgslid.es/docs/web-uploader.md#keep)
- [Permissions and data](https://svgslid.es/docs/permissions-privacy.md#web-uploader)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/web-uploader-link-expired (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 20, 2026.

# FIX: Inserted shapes landed away from the pointer in versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1

Article ID: Q100115. Last reviewed: November 20, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.

Versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 estimated the position from the size of the window, which was off when Slides was zoomed or its panels were resized. Version 1.2.0 measures the slide itself and centres the graphic on the point you click.

## Symptoms

In version 1.0.0 or 1.0.1 the shapes land some distance from where you clicked. The error grows when Slides is zoomed in, or when the filmstrip or toolbar is not at its default size.

## Cause

Those versions did not read the slide's position. They estimated it from the window size, assuming Slides' default layout.

## Resolution

Update to version 1.2.0 or later. See [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#updates).

## Status

Fixed in version 1.2.0. The extension now measures the slide you have open. In testing, an inserted graphic was centred within 2 pixels of the point clicked.

## More information

Version 1.2.0 also corrects a related fault in which visiting another slide first could throw off both placement and the editor.

## See also

- [Version 1.2.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-2-0.md)
- [Inserting SVG files](https://svgslid.es/docs/insert-svg.md#size)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/shapes-land-away-from-pointer (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 20, 2026.

# PRB: The toolbar does not appear

Article ID: Q100116. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, version 1.3.0 and later.

The toolbar is part of version 1.3.0 and shows only on a Google Slides presentation open for editing. Check the installed version, reload the tab, and look for the round button at the left edge of the slide canvas: the toolbar starts closed.

## Symptoms

There is no round button and no toolbar at the left of the slide.

## Cause and resolution

| Cause | Do this |
|---|---|
| The installed version is earlier than 1.3.0. | Check the version. See [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#check-version). Chrome updates on its own once the Chrome Web Store has published the new version. |
| The tab was open before the extension was installed or updated. | Reload the tab. |
| The toolbar is closed. | It is one round button when closed. Click it, or press Option+\. |
| Edit Shape is open. | The editor's own toolbar takes the same place. Click **Done** or **Cancel**. |
| Slides is in full-screen view. | Leave full screen. |
| The window is very small. | Make the window larger. The toolbar hides when the canvas is too small to hold it. |
| The page is not a presentation open for editing. | The extension runs only in the Slides editor. |

## See also

- [The toolbar](https://svgslid.es/docs/toolbar.md)
- [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md)
- [HOWTO: Find which version of the extension is installed](https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/which-version.md)

# HOWTO: Find which version of the extension is installed

Article ID: Q100117. Last reviewed: November 24, 2026.

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0.

Type chrome://extensions in Chrome's address bar and find SVG to Slides. The version number is beside the name. On the slide, versions 1.3.0 and later show a round toolbar button at the left of the canvas, and in version 1.4.0 the paint bucket opens a colour panel.

**To check the version**

1. In Chrome's address bar, type `chrome://extensions` and press Enter.
2. Find **SVG to Slides**. The version number is shown beside the name.

## Telling versions apart on the slide

| Version | What you see in Google Slides |
|---|---|
| 1.4.0 | The toolbar's paint bucket opens the extension's own colour panel, and works with nothing selected. |
| 1.3.0, 1.3.1 | A round button at the left edge of the slide canvas. It opens the toolbar. The paint bucket opens Slides' own colour menu. |
| 1.2.0 | No toolbar. Double-clicking a shape shows an **Edit Shape** button. |
| 1.0.0, 1.0.1 | Neither. Dropping an SVG ends with a prompt to press Command+V. |

## More information

Chrome installs new versions on its own, usually within a few hours of their release. See [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#updates) and [Version history](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes.md).

## See also

- [Installing and updating](https://svgslid.es/docs/install.md#check-version)
- [Version history](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes.md)

Source: https://svgslid.es/docs/kb/which-version (SVG to Slides Documentation, Knowledge Base). Last reviewed November 24, 2026.

# Release notes and version history

Applies to: SVG to Slides Chrome extension, versions 1.0.0 through 1.4.0; SVG to Slides Web Uploader; SVG to Slides Workspace Add-on.

Version 1.4.0 is the current release of the Chrome extension. It adds a colour panel with opacity and an eyedropper, a gradient builder, Replace a colour across a slide or the whole presentation, live preview, and image masks that keep their shape. SVG gradients and transparency now come across on import. Each release has a technical changelog below.

## Chrome extension versions

| Version | Date | What it added | Download | Installed | Chrome permissions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1.4.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-4-0.md) | November 24, 2026 | Colour panel, gradient builder, text colour, Replace a colour, live preview, masks that keep their shape, the picture adjustable under its mask, gradients and transparency on import | 434 KB | 1.3 MB | storage |
| 1.3.1 | November 2026 | Outline icon sets convert (strokes set on the root element), round caps and joins, colours from CSS classes, currentColor, hsl(), clip paths, use and symbol | 399 KB | 1.1 MB | storage |
| [1.3.0](https://svgslid.es/docs/release-notes/1-3-0.md) | November 2026 | Toolbar, pen, snapping, image masks, combine, one-press undo, instant align, Layers, outline stroke and text, command palette, full-precision points, JavaScript converter | 392 KB | 1.1 MB | storage |
